item.title: Thoma Bravo's Proofpoint to buy Varonis Systems in $6.3 billion all-cash deal
item.description: Thoma Bravo-owned cybersecurity company Proofpoint will buy data security firm Varonis Systems in an all-cash deal valued at about $6.3 billion, the companies said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Thoma Bravo-owned cybersecurity company Proofpoint will buy data security firm Varonis Systems (VRNS.O) in an all-cash deal valued at about $6.3 billion, the companies said on Thursday. Under the agreement, Varonis shareholders will receive $49.75 per share in cash, a 52% premium to the company's closing share price on June 22, the day before speculation about a possible sale first emerged, the companies said. The offer values Varonis' equity at $5.71 billion. Its shares rose about 2.7% in extended trading. The deal, expected to close in the first half of 2027, comes as businesses ramp up spending on cybersecurity to combat cybercrime, where AI is being increasingly used to steal data. Miami-based Varonis offers digital security services, including data classification on cloud storage systems and employee behavior tracking. "Our mission is to secure AI and the data that powers it. By joining forces with Proofpoint, we can achieve this mission faster than ever," Varonis co-founder and CEO Yaki Faitelson said. Reuters had [USN:L4N44U1Q6 TEXT:"reported in September"] that Proofpoint was in discussions to acquire Varonis Systems. In June, media outlets had reported that Varonis was weighing a sale after fielding takeover interest from private equity firms, sending the company's shares surging about 30%. Proofpoint, which sells software that helps companies defend against cyberattacks, was [USN:L4N2MJ2UJ TEXT:"bought"] by Thoma Bravo in 2021 in a take-private deal that valued the company at about $12.3 billion. Goldman Sachs & Co was the financial advisor to Varonis, while BofA Securities, Morgan Stanley & Co, J.P. Morgan Securities, UBS Securities, and Mizuho Securities USA advised Proofpoint. Varonis said it will announce its financial results for the third quarter on November 3, but will not hold an earnings conference call.

item.title: Monedas cierran mixtas en medio de retroceso del dólar tras datos EEUU
item.description: Las principales monedas de América Latina registraron un cierre dispar el jueves, en medio de un ligero retroceso del dólar en los mercados globales, tras una serie de datos de la economía de Estados Unidos que no dieron mayores luces sobre los próximos pasos de la Reserva Federal en materia de tasas de interés.
item.dc:creator: Froilan Romero
item.content:encoded: Las principales monedas de América Latina registraron un cierre dispar el jueves, en medio de un ligero retroceso del dólar en los mercados globales, tras una serie de datos de la economía de Estados Unidos que no dieron mayores luces sobre los próximos pasos de la Reserva Federal en materia de tasas de interés. * El índice de precios al productor (IPP) para demanda final de Estados Unidos subió un 1,3% en septiembre, reportó el Departamento del Trabajo, lo que estuvo muy por encima de las estimaciones de analistas que esperaban un aumento del 0,5%, de acuerdo a un sondeo realizado por Reuters. * El miércoles se reavivaron las expectativas de un alza de tasas de la Fed al reportarse que los precios al consumidor se aceleraron en septiembre debido al aumento de los costos de la gasolina, y las presiones sobre los precios se extendieron más allá del sector energético, lo que suscitó la preocupación de que la inflación subyacente pudiera ser persistente. * No obstante, la presidenta de la Fed de San Francisco, Mary Daly, dijo que probablemente serían necesarias nuevas subidas de tasas, pero señaló que no era necesario actuar en la reunión de octubre, mientras que la vicepresidenta de Supervisión, Michelle Bowman, dijo que aún había tiempo para esperar. * Otros datos de la economía estadounidense dados a conocer el jueves mostraron que las [USN:L6N4610WU TEXT:"ventas minoristas"] aumentaron más de lo esperado en septiembre y un leve aumento en las solicitudes de [USN:L6N4610X3 TEXT:"subsidio por desempleo"], en un contexto de bajos niveles de despidos que mantienen estable el mercado laboral. * El índice dólar , que compara al billete verde contra una canasta de seis importantes monedas, retrocedía alrededor de un 0,2%. * El peso mexicano cotizaba cerca del cierre en 18,4151 unidades dólar, con un alza del 0,35%. * El principal índice accionario S&P/BMV IPC (.MXX) , que integran las 35 empresas más líquidas del mercado mexicano, subía un 1,3%, a 67.656,89 puntos. * El real brasileño se depreció un 1,17%, a 5,0885 unidades por dólar, mientras que el índice Bovespa (.BVSP) de la bolsa B3 de Sao Paulo cedió un 1,13%, a 204.167,75 puntos. * Las ventas minoristas de Brasil aumentaron menos de lo previsto en agosto, según datos publicados el jueves por la agencia de estadística IBGE, ya que las elevadas tasas de interés siguieron lastrando la demanda de los consumidores en la mayor economía de América Latina. * En Argentina, el peso mayorista se observó estable en 1.513,50 unidades por dólar , contra una compra diaria de 182 millones de dólares por parte del banco central (BCRA). Estas intervenciones oficiales suman 574 millones de dólares en los últimos tres días. * El Tesoro argentino viene de colocar títulos por un valor efectivo de 6,61 billones de pesos (unos 4.367,4 millones de dólares) en una licitación interna para refinanciar vencimientos de corto plazo. * Los títulos públicos extrabursátiles quedaron con un sesgo positivo del 0,1% en promedio, contra un derrumbe del 1,2% previo, al tiempo que las acciones del índice líder S&P Merval (.MERV) ganaron un 0,82% al cierre, desde el 1,16% negativo del miércoles. * El peso chileno , subió un 0,25%, a 982,50/982,80 por dólar. En tanto, el principal índice de la bolsa de comercio de Santiago, el IPSA (.SPIPSA) , subió un 0,05%, a 10.971,88 puntos. * El peso colombiano cerró con avance de un 0,43% a 3.170 unidades por dólar, mientras que en la bolsa el índice accionario MSIC COLCAP (.COLCAP) se desvalorizó un 0,06% a 2.580,78 puntos. * "El peso conserva un sesgo neutral a ligeramente alcista, limitado por menores tasas en Estados Unidos, pero presionado por la caída del petróleo y la debilidad regional", indicó una nota de la correduría Acciones y Valores, en Bogotá. * La moneda peruana, el sol , se apreció un 0,47% a 3,4220/3,4230 unidades por dólar. Por su parte, la Bolsa de Lima (.MXNUAMPESCPGPE) mejoraba un 0,94% a 1.585,01 puntos. * [USN:L1N4610R9 TEXT:"La economía de Perú"] creció un 3,23% interanual en agosto, levemente por debajo de las expectativas, en medio de un buen desempeño principalmente de los sectores de construcción y comercio pese a los efectos del fenómeno climático de El Niño, dijo el jueves la oficina estatal de estadística INEI.

item.title: UK's Streeting says he and Hegseth welcomed Starlink restoration in Ukraine
item.description: Britain's defense minister said he and US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth welcomed the restoration of the Starlink service in Ukraine in talks on Thursday, and he stressed the need to move forward in supporting Kyiv following renewed discord between the US and Ukrainian leaders.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain's defense minister said he and US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth welcomed the restoration of the Starlink service in Ukraine in talks on Thursday, and he stressed the need to move forward in supporting Kyiv following [USN:L6N4610BB TEXT:"renewed discord"] between the US and Ukrainian leaders. In an appearance on Fox News' "The Story with Martha MacCallum," Wes Streeting said it was "not the first time we've seen a falling out between President Trump and President Zelenskiy." "It is, I think, important after events of recent days that we move forward in a collective spirit," he said, adding that he had quoted Saint Francis of Assisi in his meeting with Hegseth at the Pentagon: "Where there is discord, may we bring harmony." "The UK sees our role and responsibility at times like this to bring our friends back together again," Streeting said. "We need President Trump engaged on Ukraine. He has been, and the diplomatic track is as important in ending the war as making sure Ukraine has the weapons it needs to see off Russian aggression," he said. Ukraine said Elon Musk's SpaceX had [USN:L8N4600M6 TEXT:"restricted Starlink services on Wednesday"], hampering the country's attack and air-defense drone missions as worsening ties with Washington have fueled concerns over US battlefield support. Musk, the CEO of SpaceX (SPCX.O) , which operates Starlink, said the US government controlled the system's speeds. Streeting was asked if the Pentagon restricted offensive and defensive capability for Ukraine in order to prevent strikes on Russian energy installations. He replied, referring to his talks with Hegseth: "That's not my understanding. We didn't really get into why the service interruption had happened. We did reflect briefly on the fact that it had been restored and welcome that." Streeting said he was not going to speculate on why the interruption happened. He said his conversation with Hegseth was "very much about looking forward and building on the support that the UK, the US, and our allies have given to Ukraine, helping over what will be a challenging winter period to hold the line." Trump has long had a testy relationship with Zelenskiy and publicly berated him in the White House in February 2025. But his sharp turn against Kyiv in recent days has little precedent. He first angered Ukraine last week by abruptly lifting sanctions on Russian diesel, and then called for Zelenskiy to be replaced. Ukraine [USN:FWN4610DW TEXT:"struck a Russian oil refinery"] on Thursday, after Zelenskiy said Kyiv was "done" supporting a ceasefire on energy targets announced by Trump and ignored by Russia.

item.title: Cacau se mantém próximo da máxima de um mês conforme demanda dispara
item.description: Os futuros do cacau oscilaram perto da maior cotação em um mês nesta quinta-feira, após a publicação de dados de demanda da Ásia e da Europa acima do esperado, enquanto o açúcar se manteve próximo da maior cotação em 19 meses.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Os futuros do cacau oscilaram perto da maior cotação em um mês nesta quinta-feira, após a publicação de dados de demanda da Ásia e da Europa acima do esperado, enquanto o açúcar se manteve próximo da maior cotação em 19 meses. CACAU * O cacau de Londres fechou com alta de £45, ou 1%, a £4.362 por tonelada, após atingir uma máxima de um mês de £4.499 na quarta-feira. * O processamento de cacau na Europa no terceiro trimestre, um indicador da demanda, subiu 3,2% em relação ao mesmo período do ano anterior, segundo dados divulgados anteriormente, enquanto o processamento na Ásia no terceiro trimestre cresceu 29,22%. * A corretora StoneX havia previsto uma queda de 2,6% na Europa e um aumento de 17,3% na Ásia. * Dados sobre o processamento da Costa do Marfim divulgados nesta quarta-feira mostraram um aumento de 46,6% em relação ao mesmo período do ano anterior em setembro. A StoneX havia previsto um aumento de 27,2%. * O mercado aguarda agora os dados de moagem da América do Norte, a serem divulgados ainda nesta sessão, com a StoneX prevendo uma queda de 0,2%. * Além disso, o tempo seco na Costa do Marfim, principal produtora, e em partes de Gana, segunda maior produtora, também está sustentando os preços do cacau, intensificando as preocupações com o fenômeno climático El Niño. * O contrato de futuros de cacau de Nova York subiu 1,7%, para US$5.831 por tonelada, após ter atingido na quarta-feira a máxima mensal de US$6.023. AÇÚCAR * O contrato de açúcar bruto fechou com alta de 0,29 centavos, ou 1,4%, a 21,13 centavos por libra-peso, após atingir na quarta-feira uma máxima de 19 meses de 21,29. * O preço do açúcar está sendo impulsionado pelo excesso de chuvas associadas ao El Niño no Brasil, o que desacelerou a produção em setembro e reduziu o teor de sacarose na cana. * O governo brasileiro informou nesta quinta-feira que a produção de açúcar na região centro-sul do país caiu 6% na segunda quinzena de setembro, para 2,86 milhões de toneladas. * Enquanto isso, a Europa sofreu uma grave seca neste verão, que prejudicou a safra de beterraba, enquanto a Índia, segundo maior produtor, foi atingida pela seca associada ao El Niño. * O preço do açúcar branco subiu 1,1%, para US$561,10 por tonelada. CAFÉ * O preço do café arábica fechou em queda de 3,25 centavos, ou 1,1%, a US$2,948 por libra-peso, após ter atingido a maior cotação da semana na quarta-feira. * As exportações de café de Uganda caíram 13,7% em agosto, já que uma seca prolongada reduziu a safra em algumas regiões. * Os estoques certificados pela ICE caíram nos últimos três dias, atingindo apenas 238.976 sacas nesta quinta-feira, embora os participantes do mercado esperem que o café chegue em breve para recomendação. * O preço do café robusta caiu 3,1%, para US$3.375 por tonelada.

item.title: S&P 500 fecha em alta, com operadores migrando da IA para setor de saúde
item.description: O S&P 500 fechou em alta nesta quinta-feira, recuperando-se das perdas iniciais, à medida que os investidores, preocupados com as ações do setor de IA, passaram a apostar na Eli Lilly, na UnitedHealth e em outras ações dos setores de saúde e de bens de consumo.
item.dc:creator: Noel Randewich, Sruthi Shankar
item.content:encoded: O S&P 500 fechou em alta nesta quinta-feira, recuperando-se das perdas iniciais, à medida que os investidores, preocupados com as ações do setor de IA, passaram a apostar na Eli Lilly, na UnitedHealth e em outras ações dos setores de saúde e de bens de consumo. Várias ações do setor de tecnologia caíram, à medida que os investidores analisavam minuciosamente as empresas relacionadas à IA, cujo endividamento as deixa vulneráveis ao aumento das taxas de juros. A farmacêutica Eli Lilly (LLY.N) subiu mais de 3%, a UnitedHealth (UNH.N) registrou alta de 2,8% e o Walmart subiu 1,4% após elevações nos ratings pelo Deutsche Bank. Essas três empresas contribuíram fortemente para o ganho do S&P 500 no pregão. A Nvidia (NVDA.O) recuou 1,8% depois que a fabricante de chips TSMC (2330.TW) adotou um tom cauteloso em relação a 2027, apesar de ter divulgado o sexto lucro trimestral recorde consecutivo, impulsionado pela forte demanda alimentada pela IA. A Dell Technologies (DELL.N) tombou 6,9% e a Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE.N) recuou 7,1%, com ambas as fabricantes de servidores ampliando as perdas acentuadas do pregão anterior, relacionadas a preocupações com empresas de IA expostas a custos de financiamento mais elevados. O rendimento dos títulos do Tesouro de 10 anos recuou, mas permaneceu próximo de máximas de vários anos, com os investidores preocupados com a inflação relacionada aos altos preços do petróleo. “O custo para financiar tudo, seja uma nova casa ou um gigantesco data center, está subindo, e isso tem implicações para muitos setores no mercado de ações”, disse Jed Ellerbroek, gestor de portfólio da Argent Capital Management, em St. Louis. “As ações com melhor desempenho hoje são as de empresas não cíclicas e defensivas.” O índice de chips Philadelphia (.SOX) , caiu 0,9%, registrando queda pela sétima sessão consecutiva. O S&P 500 subiu 0,33%, encerrando o pregão em 7.744,06 pontos. O Nasdaq teve variação positiva de 0,08%, para 26.713,03 pontos, enquanto o Dow Jones Industrial Average registrou alta de 1,08%, para 52.177,69 pontos. Oito dos 11 índices setoriais do S&P 500 subiram, liderados pelo setor de saúde (.SPXHC) , com alta de 1,84%, seguido por um ganho de 1,71% no setor de materiais (.SPLRCM) . Depois de atingir uma alta recorde na semana passada, o S&P 500 continua com alta de cerca de 13% em 2026, com a maior parte desse ganho impulsionado por ações relacionadas à IA. Dados divulgados nesta quinta-feira mostraram que os preços ao produtor nos EUA registraram o maior aumento em 4 anos e meio em setembro, em meio ao aumento dos custos de bens e serviços — o mais recente indício de que a inflação está se expandindo para além dos produtos energéticos. Os dados de inflação ao consumidor, mais altos do que o esperado, divulgados na quarta-feira, alimentaram as expectativas de novos aumentos nas taxas de juros pelo Federal Reserve dos EUA, contribuindo para uma onda de vendas em Wall Street. “Há uma pequena rotação ocorrendo entre as empresas de maior porte, mas já vimos isso antes. Parece que isso surge a cada dois meses e temos as preocupações com a IA”, disse Joe Saluzzi, codiretor de operações com ações da Themis Trading em Chatham, Nova Jersey. Os operadores de taxas de juros estão precificando uma chance de 67% de que o Fed aumente as taxas de juros em sua reunião de política monetária de dezembro, acima da probabilidade de 62% registrada na quarta-feira, de acordo com a ferramenta FedWatch da CME. As ações da Rocket Lab (RKLB.O) tombaram 6,6% depois que a empresa espacial informou que o lançamento inaugural de seu novo foguete Neutron, de maior porte, foi adiado para o próximo ano. A FMC (FMC.N) despencou mais de 30% depois que a empresa de agroquímicos reduziu drasticamente suas projeções para o terceiro trimestre.

item.title: El alza del diésel comienza a afectar a otros precios en Estados Unidos
item.description: El vertiginoso aumento del precio del diésel es evidente para los estadounidenses cada vez que repostan sus autos, todoterrenos y camionetas, aunque solo una pequeña parte de los conductores posee un vehículo diésel, por lo que podrían pensar que se están librando del alza del precio.
item.dc:creator: Dan Burns
item.content:encoded: El vertiginoso aumento del precio del diésel es evidente para los estadounidenses cada vez que repostan sus autos, todoterrenos y camionetas, aunque solo una pequeña parte de los conductores posee un vehículo diésel, por lo que podrían pensar que se están librando del alza del precio. Los datos sobre la inflación al por mayor publicados el jueves por el Departamento de Trabajo mostraron que los precios al productor en Estados Unidos subieron mucho más de lo esperado en septiembre, lo que augura una inflación aún más acusada para los consumidores en las próximas semanas y meses, a medida que los costos les repercutan. Las pruebas del impacto de los altos precios de la energía, en particular los precios récord del diésel, están presentes en todo el informe de 34 páginas. "El gasóleo es el combustible motor de la economía", escribió Oxford Economics. Las siguientes son algunas de las formas en que el diésel o gasóleo está impulsando la inflación de los precios al productor en Estados Unidos y cómo amenaza con acelerar más, y pronto, varios costos para los consumidores. EN LA PUERTA DE LA CASA Tanto si se come o se bebe, en algún punto del trayecto un camión lo ha transportado, ya sea hasta el lugar donde se compra o hasta la puerta de la casa. La gran mayoría de los vehículos de la flota de transporte de mercancías de Estados Unidos funcionan con gasóleo. Así que, cuando los precios del diésel más que se duplican, como ha ocurrido durante el último año, el costo de transportar todo aumenta y, en breve, los transportistas empiezan a exigir precios más altos por el servicio. En septiembre, el indicador del Índice de Precios al Productor relativo al costo del transporte de mercancías por camión subió un 19% interanual, el mayor incremento en algo más de cuatro años. Es más, el cobro por el transporte de mercancías está reaccionando mucho más rápidamente al repunte del diésel que durante el alza que siguió a la pandemia de la COVID-19. Esto porque la economía se encuentra ahora en una situación mucho mejor, con una tasa de desempleo en un mínimo histórico del 4,2%, lo que sustenta una demanda sólida. Además, el precio absoluto del combustible es más del doble de lo que era cuando comenzó la recuperación tras la pandemia. DE LA GRANJA A LA MESA El diésel es fundamental para la agricultura, ya que mueve los tractores y las cosechadoras y, nuevamente, los camiones que transportan los cultivos a los supermercados y restaurantes. Aunque los aumentos en el costo de los alimentos para el consumidor final, tanto en el Índice de Precios al Productor (IPP) como en el Índice de Precios al Consumidor (IPC), fueron bastante moderados en septiembre, en las fases anteriores de la cadena de suministro alimentario están aumentando rápidamente. El promedio de los insumos alimentarios en las etapas uno y dos de lo que el IPP denomina "demanda intermedia" -que refleja los propios costos energéticos de los productores y los implícitos de elementos clave que usan los agricultores, como fertilizantes y otros productos químicos agrícolas- subió un 15,6% respecto de septiembre del año anterior, lo que supone el mayor incremento en unos cuatro años. Los precios de los productos forrajeros sensibles al valor de la energía, como el maíz, el heno, las semillas de heno y las semillas oleaginosas, se dispararon más de un 25% interanual. Si nos guiamos por la historia, los hogares deberían prepararse para un aumento aún mayor de los precios en los supermercados en los próximos meses. "Prevemos un repunte de la inflación de los alimentos a finales de este año", dijo Matthew Martin, economista sénior de Oxford especializado en Estados Unidos, tras la publicación del informe del IPP. ENERGÍA Y IPC La economía estadounidense consume hoy mucha menos energía que durante las crisis del petróleo de la década de 1970, pero esto sigue teniendo un impacto en los precios en general, y más cuanto más tiempo sigan altos. Categorías del IPP como los materiales para la fabricación -insumos que, a su vez, absorben los mayores costos del gasóleo para su producción y distribución- están aumentando a tasas anuales de dos dígitos. Los productores deben asumir el impacto en sus márgenes o repercutirlos. SE ACERCA LA NAVIDAD La subida del diésel amenaza con encarecer la próxima temporada navideña y ya es un factor determinante en uno de los productos básicos más importantes de la temporada: los juguetes. Los precios de los juguetes están expuestos, entre otras cosas, a unos costos de envío más altos, y que en septiembre anotaron su mayor subida intermensual de la historia.

item.title: Crucial to give Ukraine all means needed to defend population, infrastructure, France's Macron says
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron said on Thursday that it was crucial to give Ukraine all the means it needs to defend and protect its civilian population and its infrastructure, after he met in Brussels with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: French President Emmanuel Macron said on Thursday that it was crucial to give Ukraine all the means it needs to defend and protect its civilian population and its infrastructure, after he met in Brussels with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy. Zelenskiy, writing on Telegram, described his conversation with Macron as "very much to the point" and said Ukraine valued France for "helping as much as possible to find responses to Russian escalation." Zelenskiy said France would be providing more assistance for Ukraine's aviation in the coming month and both sides were keen to speed up work on the FREYJA project for a European anti-ballistic missile defence system.

item.title: Senate Republicans plan post-election blitz to confirm Trump's judicial nominees
item.description: US Senate Republicans are laying the groundwork to confirm as many of President Donald Trump's judicial nominees as possible in the weeks after the November 3 midterm elections, as the chance of Democrats flipping the chamber looms.
item.dc:creator: Nate Raymond
item.content:encoded: US Senate Republicans are laying the groundwork to confirm as many of President Donald Trump's judicial nominees as possible in the weeks after the November 3 [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterm elections"], as the chance of Democrats flipping the chamber looms. Republican Senate Judiciary Committee Chair Chuck Grassley plans to hold two judicial nomination hearings during the Senate's two-week November session, after the election but before new members are sworn in, a person familiar with the process said on Thursday. That's a break from the traditional pattern of holding only one such hearing every two weeks. Six nominees are awaiting a hearing, many of whom would be eligible to appear at the November 10 hearing. Another hearing is set for November 18, and Trump potentially could announce additional nominees before then. The back-to-back sessions would allow the panel to advance those nominees to the floor and have them voted on by the full Senate in December during the final weeks of the current Congress. "Wherever there are judicial vacancies, President Trump will select highly qualified nominees with great respect for our Constitution and rule of law to be confirmed expeditiously," White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis said in a statement. The nomination hearings, which were first reported by Punchbowl News, were set over the objections of the panel's top Democrat, Senator Dick Durbin of Illinois, who in a statement warned his Republican colleagues that the move could be used against them in the future under a Democratic president. "The chairman’s plan to hold two back-to-back nomination hearings one week apart without minority consent in November departs from longstanding committee practice and establishes a new precedent that will allow Democrats to process nominees more quickly in a future Democratic administration," Durbin said. Trump's low approval ratings, voter concern over high prices and dissatisfaction with the Iran war have led many analysts and opinion polls to predict significant Democratic gains in the elections, giving them a chance to win control of the Senate, which Republicans now control with a 53-47 majority. If Democrats win control of the Senate, the White House would face a [USN:L1N45A0IR TEXT:"harder road"] to secure confirmation of judicial nominees named by Trump, who during his first and second terms helped shift the judiciary's ideological balance to the right and secure a 6-3 conservative majority on the US Supreme Court. Trump secured confirmation of 234 judicial nominees in his first term. Since Trump's return to the White House in January 2025, the Republican-led Senate has confirmed 56 judges, including 10 on the influential appeals courts. Among the six nominees awaiting hearings before the Senate Judiciary Committee is [USN:L1N45N0RH TEXT:"Todd Butler"], a partner at law firm Phelps Dunbar who was nominated to serve on the New Orleans-based 5th US Circuit Court of Appeals, which is considered the most conservative appeals court in the nation. One nominee, Samuel Adkisson of the White House Counsel's Office, is [USN:L1N45M124 TEXT:"being held up"] by a member of Trump's own party, Senator Marsha Blackburn of Tennessee. She has declined without explanation to return a so-called blue slip allowing for his consideration for a federal judgeship in her home state. Read more: [USN:L1N4500N3 TEXT:"Trump faces tight timeline to appoint judges as midterms loom"]

item.title: Presidenta justifica drástica reducción área protegida para vaquita marina por bienestar de pescadores
item.description: La presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum justificó el jueves una drástica reducción del área protegida para la casi extinta vaquita marina, un mamífero endémico del Golfo de California, al argumentar que las comunidades pesqueras de la zona han visto afectado su bienestar por las vedas y que los pescadores no son responsables de la disminución de la especie.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum justificó el jueves una drástica reducción del área protegida para la casi extinta vaquita marina, un mamífero endémico del Golfo de California, al argumentar que las comunidades pesqueras de la zona han visto afectado su bienestar por las vedas y que los pescadores no son responsables de la disminución de la especie. El Gobierno publicó el miércoles un nuevo acuerdo regulatorio que sustituye al de 2020 y reduce en 86%, a 1,562 kilómetros cuadrados, el área donde están prohibidas las redes de enmalle en el Alto Golfo de California. Con ello, más de 9,500 kilómetros cuadrados quedan abiertos a la pesca con esas redes, incluidas las agalleras, que representan un riesgo para las vaquitas. El acuerdo de 2020 abarcaba 11,106 kilómetros cuadrados. El documento, publicado en el Diario Oficial de la Federación, indica que "el Gobierno de México promueve la pesca sustentable y sostenible en el Alto Golfo de California". Agrega que la modificación se basó en un análisis que tomó en cuenta los avistamientos de ejemplares, las opiniones del sector pesquero y los informes y propuestas del Comité Internacional para la Recuperación de la Vaquita (CIRVA), órgano científico asesor del Gobierno. "Se hizo un estudio, de manera muy importante, de cómo se protege la biodiversidad y, al mismo tiempo, se permite que los pescadores puedan vivir adecuadamente", dijo Sheinbaum en su conferencia matutina al ser consultada sobre la reducción del polígono. "Una parte de veda (es) necesaria para la protección de la biodiversidad, pero muchas veces muchos pescadores que viven de la pesca, al tener tanto tiempo de veda, pueden tener una problemática sencillamente de bienestar". Científicos y organizaciones ambientalistas han expresado preocupación por la ampliación del área disponible para estas redes, un cambio que ya se discutía desde hace meses. Temen que las vaquitas, como ha sucedido, queden atrapadas incidentalmente en redes, muchas de ellas ilegales, usadas para capturar totoaba, un pez cuya vejiga natatoria se vende en Asia por altas sumas. La especie continúa en peligro crítico de extinción y su población se mantiene en niveles extremadamente bajos. En el monitoreo de septiembre de 2025 se observaron entre siete y 10 individuos, incluida al menos una cría, según divulgó el Gobierno en octubre de ese año. Según el acuerdo, dentro del polígono restante se mantiene la prohibición permanente de las redes de enmalle. También continúa una zona de tolerancia cero de 225 kilómetros cuadrados, donde están prohibidas la pesca y la navegación, salvo excepciones reguladas, incluido un canal para el tránsito de embarcaciones menores de pesca. México ha intentado frenar la pesca ilegal de totoaba en el Golfo de California para proteger a la vaquita marina. Entre las medidas están reformas legales para castigar la pesca de especies en veda, restricciones a la pesca y operativos conjuntos en el Golfo de California que han asegurado miles de metros de redes de enmalle y decenas de ejemplares marinos capturados. "Con apenas un puñado de vaquitas, es absolutamente impactante que el Gobierno desmantele las protecciones en lugar de intensificar la ayuda a estas pequeñas marsopas", dijo Alex Olivera, representante en México del Center for Biological Diversity. "En lugar de reforzar la aplicación de la ley, México está normalizando la pesca ilegal que el Gobierno no ha podido, o no ha querido, detener. Estas nuevas reglas abren la mayor parte del hábitat restante de la vaquita al arte de pesca que las mata".

item.title: Petey Halpin, dominant pitchers push Guardians to 2-1 ALCS lead over Rays
item.description: CLEVELAND -- Petey Halpin reacted to the most important hit of his young career by flipping his bat high into the sky. The rest of the Cleveland Guardians saved their wildest celebrations for the postgame.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: CLEVELAND -- Petey Halpin reacted to the most important hit of his young career by flipping his bat high into the sky. The rest of the Cleveland Guardians saved their wildest celebrations for the postgame. Halpin's go-ahead, two-run homer in the fifth inning off Griffin Jax was the difference in Game 3 of the American League Championship Series, giving Cleveland a 3-2 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays on Thursday afternoon. The Guardians now lead the best-of-seven series 2-1. With the next two games at home, they could wrap up the pennant and book a trip to the World Series without a return to Florida. Halpin's first postseason home run traveled 385 feet over the fence in right, scoring Patrick Bailey to give the Guardians a 3-2 advantage. It was the first homer allowed by Jax since Sept. 9, prompting Halpin to send his bat comically airborne. "I thought I got more of it, I guess, and maybe I was a little tense, so I kind of threw it," Halpin said of the bat flip that ignited the non-sellout crowd of 30,101. "But it's only got to go a little bit over the wall, so that was cool." After Halpin gave AL Central champion Cleveland the lead, its pitching staff took over. Staff ace Gavin Williams and four relievers combined on a three-hitter, striking out 13 to extend their total to 102, an MLB record through eight postseason games. Williams (2-0) struck out nine over five innings, allowing two runs on two hits and a walk. The right-hander leads postseason pitchers with 33 strikeouts in just 16 2/3 innings over four appearances. "I keep telling myself, 'Don't let the moment get too big,'" Williams said. "I've just got to keep the same routine and keep doing the same thing and I'll be good. "Everybody here is just gritty. That's the big thing. And knowing what you need to do in the right situations." Cade Smith pitched a perfect final 1 1/3 innings for his second save of the series. Daniel Espino, Erik Sabrowski and Hunter Gaddis also saw action as Cleveland began a three-game homestand in the series. Jax (0-1) worked four-plus innings, giving up three runs on five hits. The right-hander struck out two and walked a pair, but was left lamenting his lack of control on the sinker that Halpin sent over the fence. "He does a good job handling off-speed, so it was the right pitch," Jax said. "Just the wrong location." Tampa Bay took a 2-1 lead in the fourth on Chandler Simpson's two-run triple to right. Yandy Diaz and Victor Mesa Jr. scored on the hit that landed just inside the foul line, making Simpson 3-for-6 in his career against Williams. "It was a real good fastball, but I was ready for that," Simpson said. "I got a good pitch that I got the barrel on. The fact that we were down at the time, it gave us a lot of momentum." The Rays' three hits were their fewest in an ALCS game in three appearances. Their 2-1 series deficit is the first time they have trailed in the round after three games. Williams, who carried a no-hitter into the sixth in Game 5 of the AL Division Series against the Chicago White Sox, retired the first nine batters before Diaz doubled leading off the fourth. "Look, we're not a team that strikes out a lot, but I think our swings have actually been pretty good," Diaz said through a translator. "We just need to put the ball in play." Nathaniel Lowe doubled in the second, driving in Jo Adell to put Cleveland up 1-0. Adell had been called out on strikes by umpire Bill Miller, but challenged it and drew a walk. Diaz appeared in his franchise postseason-record 31st game for the Rays. Jax, an Air Force Reserve captain, became the first pitcher to graduate from a United States military academy and start a playoff game. --Brian Dulik, Field Level Media

item.title: KFC picks Coca-Cola as US soda supplier, ditches longtime partner PepsiCo
item.description: Fast-food chain KFC on Thursday signed Coca-Cola as its beverage partner for US stores, bringing to a close a relationship with PepsiCo that dates back about four decades.
item.dc:creator: Juveria Tabassum
item.content:encoded: Fast-food chain KFC (YUM.N) on Thursday signed Coca-Cola (KO.N) as its beverage partner for US stores, bringing to a close a relationship with PepsiCo (PEP.O) that dates back about four decades. The loss of the beverage partnership with KFC, which has 3,718 US locations, could be a setback for PepsiCo as it works to improve soda sales in the country, while its snacks business grapples with high prices and a shift to healthier options. Higher costs have also added to concerns for PepsiCo CEO Ramon Laguarta, who said earlier this month that growth and margin recovery was taking [USN:L6N45U0N9 TEXT:"longer than planned."] The partnership began when PepsiCo acquired KFC in a bid to expand into food and snacks. While PepsiCo later spun off KFC in 1997, it continued to be a beverage partner for its parent Yum Brands. "It is just a bad look for PepsiCo... when you lose a big-name brand partner like that. This could be the optical straw that breaks the camel's back," said Jay Woods, chief market strategist at Freedom Capital Markets. "It is very rare that you have two giants in the same industry take such a different turn," he said. Freedom Capital Markets holds shares in Coca-Cola. PepsiCo is also [USN:L4N45S0OW TEXT:"under scrutiny"] from activist investor Elliott Investment Management, which disclosed a stake in the company last year, and has asked it to [USN:L4N3UP0T9 TEXT:"sell underperforming assets"] and improve its performance in North America. Yum Brands and PepsiCo just renewed agreements across Taco Bell and KFC International stores, a spokesperson for PepsiCo told Reuters. Taco Bell is a 10-year agreement, they said. PepsiCo has beverage partner agreements at sandwich chains Subway and Jersey Mike's Subs (JMKE.N) . It also runs the soda fountain at Pizza Hut, which [USN:L6N42O0TI TEXT:"left the Yum Brands umbrella"] only this year and switched to PepsiCo from Coca-Cola in 2011. In 2012, [USN:L3E8F27M7 TEXT:"PepsiCo lost Dunkin to Coca-Cola"] after a five-year run at the donut chain. Coca-Cola products will be available at KFC US restaurants by spring 2027, the company said. Financial details of the partnership were not disclosed. Coca-Cola is a long-standing beverage partner at burger chains McDonald's (MCD.N) and Wendy's (WEN.O) . The Wall Street Journal first reported the news on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter.

item.title: France, Germany near deal on car emissions, Britain 'Made in EU' status
item.description: France and Germany are nearing a deal on cars that would water down EU-wide CO2 emission targets for 2035 and open the door for Britain to be treated as a trusted partner under the EU's Made in EU rules, diplomats said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: France and Germany are nearing a deal on cars that would water down EU-wide CO2 emission targets for 2035 and open the door for Britain to be treated as a trusted partner under the EU's [USN:L6N45E0Q1 TEXT:""Made in EU" rules"], diplomats said. The European Commission [USN:L6N3XM0EA TEXT:"proposed last year"] that CO2 emissions from cars should drop by 90% from 2021 levels in 2035, but said automakers would have to close the gap to 100% by using low-carbon steel and alternative fuels. Under the Franco-German plan, which still needs to be confirmed, the target would be set at 90% without the need for any further compensatory measures. The softened target is broadly in line with the wishes of German carmakers. The joint plan also addresses an EU proposal that introduces local-content and low-carbon requirements for products bought through public procurement, public auctions or via subsidy schemes. France has been pushing for these products to be limited to those manufactured in the European Union, while other EU members, including Germany, believe other countries, including those closely linked in automotive supply chains and free trade agreement partners, should be included. The provisional Franco-German plan says that for the automotive sector "Made in Europe" should cover the EU's 27 countries and other European partners that were part of the EU internal market on January 1, 2020. That would include Britain, which left the EU single market at the end of 2020. However, the joint plan does say that this inclusion should be subject to an agreement on full reciprocity, along with "dynamic alignment with EU conditions for investment from third countries and with EU trade protection measures". That could mean Britain having to adopt the measures the EU has taken to limit imports of Chinese-built hybrid and battery electric vehicles. In Germany, the new CO2 reduction target could prove a challenge as the environment minister of the Social Democrats has suggested that the target could be cut to 95%, with a further 5-percentage-point reduction offset via low-carbon steel. Even with a Franco-German deal, the two countries still would need to convince other EU members and the European Parliament for their plans to enter into force.

item.title: Report: CFP nearing deal to expand to 24 teams in 2027
item.description: The College Football Playoff is nearing a deal to double its number of participating teams from 12 to 24, according to rights holder ESPN.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The College Football Playoff is nearing a deal to double its number of participating teams from 12 to 24, according to rights holder ESPN. The new format would come into effect in 2027 and is pending final approvals, the network reported on Thursday. "Constructive discussions with ESPN continued this week," read a statement from the CFP late Thursday. "We have enjoyed a strong partnership with ESPN since our inception and are appreciative of the productive dialogue we have had throughout the negotiating period and continuing over the last several days. We will provide additional updates on the matters of future format and media rights when appropriate." The playoff's quarterfinals and semifinals are expected to still belong to the New Year's Six bowl games (Rose, Fiesta, Sugar, Peach, Orange, Cotton) within the proposed new format, while the national championship game will likely remain in January. The CFP has used a 12-team format since 2024. From 2014 through 2023, just four teams competed in the postseason event. In March 2024, the CFP and ESPN agreed to a six-year, $7.8 billion contract, giving the network sole media rights through the 2031 season. After months of studying the pros and cons of expansion, the playoff's management committee moved forward with official discussions in September, which are ongoing. In the proposed plan, the top eight seeds receive byes, and seeds 9-16 host seeds 17-24 in the first round. The top eight then host the first-round winners. --Field Level Media

item.title: Comcast owes $213 million in video-streaming patent dispute, US jury says
item.description: A jury in Tampa, Florida, found on Thursday that Comcast owes digital television provider WhereverTV $213 million in damages for infringing a patent related to streaming video.
item.dc:creator: Blake Brittain
item.content:encoded: A jury in Tampa, Florida, found on Thursday that Comcast (CMCSA.O) owes digital television provider WhereverTV $213 million in damages for infringing a patent related to streaming video. The jury agreed with Fort Myers-based WhereverTV that Comcast's X1 set-top boxes violate its patent rights in technology for integrating cable channels with streaming services, according to a copy of the verdict provided by WhereverTV's attorneys "We remain confident that our X1 guide does not infringe WhereverTV’s patent, and we will pursue all of our legal options including appeal," Comcast said in a statement. The company also said that the verdict would have no impact on its customers WhereverTV's founder Mark Cavicchia invented the patented technology covering "novel systems for receiving, accessing, managing, and viewing digital content from different sources," the company said in a court filing The lawsuit, filed in 2018, said that Comcast integrated the technology into its X1 platform around 2012 when it was "losing subscribers and market share due to so-called cord cutters" Comcast denied the allegations and argued that the patent was invalid A Florida judge ruled that Comcast did not infringe the patent during an earlier jury trial in 2023, but the US Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit overturned his ruling in 2025 and sent the case back for a new trial The case is WhereverTV Inc v. Comcast Corp, US District Court for the Middle District of Florida, No. 2:18-cv-00529. For WhereverTV: Adam Sanderson of Reese Marketos For Comcast: Traci McKee of Faegre Drinker Biddle & Reath

item.title: India raises windfall tax on petrol, cuts duty on diesel
item.description: India has raised the windfall tax on exports of petrol and cut the duty on diesel, according to a government order issued late Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: India has raised the windfall tax on exports of petrol and cut the duty on diesel, according to a government order issued late Thursday. The export duty on petrol was raised to 2.5 rupees ($0.0263) per litre from 0.5 rupees per litre, while the duty on diesel exports was cut to 8.5 rupees per litre from 16 rupees per litre, effective October 16, the order said. India first imposed windfall taxes on fuel exports in July 2022 and withdrew them two years later. The government reintroduced the tax in March 2026 after crude prices jumped during the US-Israeli war on Iran. The export duties are currently reviewed every fortnight and adjusted in line with movements in international crude oil and petroleum product prices. ($1 = 95.0550 Indian rupees)

item.title: Diesel's surge is starting to push other prices around. Here's how
item.description: From freight to food, consumers are set to feel the heat as surging diesel prices drive up producer inflation and push costs higher across the economy.
item.dc:creator: Dan Burns
item.content:encoded: The skyrocketing price of diesel is plain for Americans to see anytime they fuel up their cars, SUVs and pickup trucks, though only a fraction of US drivers own a diesel-powered vehicle so they may think they are dodging that massive sticker shock. Think again. Wholesale inflation data from the Labor Department on Thursday showed US producer prices climbed far more than expected in September — auguring more stiff inflation at the consumer level in the weeks and months ahead as those costs get passed along. Evidence of the impact of high energy prices, record-high diesel prices in particular, was all over that 34-page readout. Why? Because, as Oxford Economics wrote recently: "Diesel is the workhorse fuel of the economy." Here are some of the ways diesel is driving up producer inflation and how that threatens to drive up a range of consumer costs further soon. GETTING IT TO YOUR DOOR If you own it, eat it or drink it, a truck was involved somewhere along the way in bringing it — either to where you picked it up or to your house. The vast majority of those vehicles in the US goods transportation fleet run on diesel. So when diesel prices more than double as they have over the last year, the cost of moving all that stuff around goes up and soon those shippers begin demanding higher prices for that service. In September, the Producer Price Index's gauge of the cost for truck transportation of freight was up by 19% year over year, the most in just over four years. What's more, those freight transportation costs are responding much faster to the surge in diesel prices than they did to the price surge following the COVID-19 pandemic. That's because the overall economy is in a much better position now than it was then, with the US jobless rate at a still historically low 4.2% supporting robust demand. Also the absolute price of the fuel is more than twice what it was as the pandemic recovery began. FARM TO TABLE Diesel is critical to farming, powering the tractors and harvesting equipment involved in producing food and again in fueling the trucks that take it to grocery stores and restaurants. While end-user consumer food cost increases in both PPI and the Consumer Price Index in September were pretty benign, costs further back in the food supply chain are rising fast. The average of food inputs at stages one and two of what PPI calls "intermediate demand" - which reflect producers' own energy costs and the energy costs embedded in producing key things farmers use like fertilizers and other agricultural chemicals — was up 15.6% from a year earlier in September, again by the most in about four years. Prices for energy-sensitive feed products like corn, hay and hayseeds and oilseeds all shot up by more than 25% year over year. If history is any guide, households should brace for yet higher grocery store prices in the months ahead. "We expect a pickup in food inflation later this year," Oxford's senior US economist Matthew Martin said after the PPI report. ENERGY & CPI The US economy is far less energy-intensive than it was during the oil shocks of the 1970s, but it is still has an impact on prices overall — and more so the longer they stay high. PPI categories like materials for manufacturing — inputs that are themselves absorbing higher diesel costs to produce and deliver — are rising at double-digit annual rates. Producers must take the hit to their margins or pass the costs along. CHRISTMAS IS COMING The diesel surge threatens to make the coming holiday season more expensive — and is already a factor in one of the season's biggest staples: Toys. Prices for toys — exposed to higher shipping costs among other things — rose in September by the most ever month over month.

item.title: Masiva marcha universitaria contra Milei concluye con incidentes en Argentina
item.description: Una multitudinaria protesta de argentinos contra el ajuste del presidente ultraliberal Javier Milei sobre la educación concluyó el jueves con incidentes con la policía frente al Congreso de la Nación.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Una multitudinaria protesta de argentinos contra el ajuste del presidente ultraliberal Javier Milei sobre la educación concluyó el jueves con incidentes con la policía frente al Congreso de la Nación. Los manifestantes, mayormente estudiantes, docentes y ciudadanos independientes, reclamaban al presidente el cumplimiento de una ley dictada por el Congreso para revertir la reducción del presupuesto universitario, que el Gobierno ha desoído pese a diversos fallos judiciales en su contra. La protesta refleja el profundo malestar de gran parte de la clase media argentina con el ajuste que el mandatario aplicó sobre la economía -en particular sobre sectores sensibles como educación y salud- para reducir la inflación. Ese disgusto se observa en la baja popularidad de Milei que muestra la mayoría de las encuestas de opinión. Autoridades de la Universidad de Buenos Aires (UBA), que cuenta con más de 300.000 estudiantes y varios premios Nobel a lo largo de su historia, estimaron que su personal perdió cerca del 30% de su salario bajo la gestión de la derecha radical. "No normalicemos el incumplimiento de la ley. Las leyes se cumplen. Siempre", publicó en redes sociales la UBA para convocar a la protesta que se desarrollaba frente al Congreso de la Nación. Con inmensas banderas y pancartas a favor de la educación pública, la multitudinaria convocatoria mantuvo paralizado el centro de la ciudad. Pero antes del acto principal hubo enfrentamientos entre la policía y un grupo minoritario situado entre los manifestantes, frente al Congreso, en Buenos Aires, que acabó con heridos y aceleró el fin de la protesta. "Nuestro reclamo es por el financiamiento, por el presupuesto universitario que hace más de 350 días que el Gobierno no cumple. Vamos a seguir luchando por la universidad pública, gratuita y de calidad", dijo a Reuters Juan Sgró, profesor de la Facultad de Artes de la Universidad Nacional de Córdoba. La protesta se replicó en otras importantes ciudades del país como Rosario y Córdoba.

item.title: BHP sues union at Spence copper mine over 'illegal' stoppages
item.description: Global miner BHP has sued the workers' union at its Spence copper mine in Chile over two work stoppages it deemed "illegal" because they occurred outside a scheduled negotiating period, a court filing seen by Reuters on Thursday showed.
item.dc:creator: Fabian Cambero, Paolo Laudani
item.content:encoded: Global miner BHP (BHP.AX) has sued the workers' union at its Spence copper mine in Chile over two work stoppages it deemed "illegal" because they occurred outside a scheduled negotiating period, a court filing seen by Reuters on Thursday showed. In the lawsuit, BHP alleged that the mine operations were "significantly" affected due to "two illegal work stoppages" in June and July, and sought compensation of roughly $8.6 million. The union aimed to pressure the mine to pay a special bonus of 5 million pesos ($5,102) per member, which was not included in the existing agreements, the lawsuit shows. The union declined to comment. BHP in a statement confirmed that it had filed the lawsuit. Spence is BHP's second-largest operation in Chile, a country where the firm runs the world's biggest copper mine Escondida. Copper mine unions in Chile, the world's biggest copper producer, often stage strikes to push for better pay and benefits, usually during contract negotiations. ($1 = 979.9300 Chilean pesos)

item.title: OpenAI, Meta caution US judiciary about risk of 'deepfake' evidence
item.description: Tech experts at OpenAI and Meta Platforms warned a federal judicial panel on Thursday that AI-generated "deepfakes" are becoming so sophisticated that it will become increasingly challenging to determine the authenticity of audio and video evidence presented at trial.
item.dc:creator: Nate Raymond
item.content:encoded: Tech experts at OpenAI and Meta Platforms (META.O) warned a federal judicial panel on Thursday that AI-generated "deepfakes" are becoming so sophisticated that it will become increasingly challenging to determine the authenticity of audio and video evidence presented at trial. The companies' representatives and other experts shared their views on the evolving technology during a meeting in Boston of the US Judicial Conference's Advisory Committee on Evidence Rules, which for three years has grappled with how to police the risks of fabricated AI-generated evidence in court. In that period alone, rapid advancements in generative AI have reached the point where fabricated videos have become difficult for both humans and software to spot, experts advised at the meeting. "AI images are only getting better, and I do not think that there will be a scientific way going forward to detect them," OpenAI policy counsel Shira Anderson told the committee. The panel has [USN:L1N41K1BT TEXT:"struggled since 2023"] with how to address authentication issues related to deepfakes and ensure that evidence known to be generated by AI meets the same reliability standards as evidence from a human expert witness. The judiciary has sought to get ahead of the issue despite a lack of evidence that it is a widespread problem. The Federal Judiciary Center, the judiciary's research arm, in March said that out of 931 judges who responded to a survey, only 15 had encountered a case in which a litigant challenged the introduction of evidence because it was a deepfake. "There's a lot of academic commentary and other commentary predicting that courts will be dealing with deepfakes, but we haven't actually seen a whole lot of that yet," said US District Judge Jesse Furman of Manhattan, who chairs the panel and on Thursday appointed a subcommittee to further examine the issue. Experts from industry, academia and government warned that the issue is far from purely hypothetical. They said the courts' ability to act as gatekeepers against fabricated AI-generated evidence is only going to become more challenging. "Media generated from frontier models, at least in the last few generations, are indistinguishable by humans from authentic or AI-generated media," said Devin Norder, director of product management at Meta. "And the cost and the time it takes to create this media really are quite trivial at this point." Major companies including OpenAI and Meta have sought to adopt tools and services aimed at verifying the validity of visual content, and new laws in California and the European Union require "watermarking" aimed at detecting deepfakes. But Anderson warned that because each company has its own system, there's no universal means to reliably detect all watermarks or verify the authenticity of visual content. "My guess is that this absolutely will continue to get better," she said. "I do not think it'll ever be bulletproof." Despite those factors, Manhattan US District Judge Valerie Caproni, a member of the committee, expressed caution about the judiciary rushing to craft an AI-specific rule to address the issue, given the lack of data indicating that such a problem was plaguing the courts. She said even if courts began to regularly confront deepfakes, current rules and laws already make it illegal to submit fraudulent evidence and allow judges determine whether evidence was forged. "We've dealt with bad actors presenting fake evidence since Cain and Abel," she said. "That's a longstanding problem." item.title: Congo Ebola outbreak spreads to new province bordering Central African Republic
item.description: The ongoing Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo has spread to a new province bordering Central African Republic, two health officials said on Thursday, posing a fresh challenge for authorities struggling to contain it.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The ongoing Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo has spread to a new province bordering Central African Republic, two health officials said on Thursday, posing a fresh challenge for authorities struggling to contain it. North Ubangi becomes the eighth province to be affected by the outbreak of the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, which was announced in mid-May and has become the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record, with more than 9,000 cases and more than 4,000 deaths confirmed. Two cases have been confirmed in North Ubangi, the officials said. They have not been officially announced by Congolese authorities. Ituri province remains the epicentre of the outbreak though cases have increased recently in North [USN:L6N45H0P8 TEXT:"Kivu"] province. Cases have also been confirmed in South Kivu, Tshopo, Haut-Uele, Bas-Uele and South Ubangi provinces. A health official in North Ubangi told Reuters on Thursday there had been a series of suspect deaths recently in a mining area in Wapinda health zone, close to the border with Bas-Uele, prompting samples to be analysed at a provincial laboratory and in Kinshasa. In addition to spreading within Congo, the outbreak has also resulted in cases in Uganda, which was declared Ebola-free in August, and in Kenya, which announced its [USN:L8N45S0GY TEXT:"first Ebola infection"] earlier this month and announced a second case - a close family member of the first one - on [USN:L6N46011B TEXT:"Wednesday"].

item.title: Volvo Cars expands automated driving partnership with Nvidia
item.description: Volvo Cars is expanding its partnership with Nvidia to develop a new generation of driver-assistance and automated-driving technology, the companies said on Thursday, as carmakers race to bring increasingly advanced hands-free driving features to market.
item.dc:creator: Marie Mannes
item.content:encoded: Volvo Cars (VOLCARb.ST) is expanding its partnership with Nvidia (NVDA.O) to [USN:L6N3Y610S TEXT:"develop"] a new generation of driver-assistance and automated-driving technology, the companies said on Thursday, as carmakers race to bring increasingly advanced hands-free driving features to market. The companies said Volvo would combine its safety systems and engineering expertise with Nvidia's artificial intelligence and computing technologies, including the Hyperion sensor, computer architecture and autonomous-driving software stack. Automakers including Mercedes-Benz, BMW and Ford have been targeting more advanced automated-driving systems, from hands-free highway driving to self-driving in limited conditions. Tesla is [USN:L6N45R0YL TEXT:"pushing"] for broader [USN:L6N45V0PF TEXT:"approval"] of its assisted-driving technology in Europe, including urban areas with an EU-wide [USN:L6N45H0TX TEXT:"vote"] possible in December. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told reporters in Stockholm that partnering with Volvo provided the chipmaker with a "tremendous opportunity" because of the automaker's rigorous safety standards. Huang said features would be rolled out gradually. "As the car earns its trust and as Volvo becomes comfortable with the capabilities of the cars, they'll continue to expand the services that are available. There's no hurry, safety first," Huang said. Besides Volvo, Nvidia has [USN:L1N3Y90FP TEXT:"partnerships"] with a wide range of automakers, including Mercedes, Jaguar Land Rover and Hyundai. Volvo CEO Hakan Samuelsson said the company would take a cautious approach to deployment. "We will never let it out under conditions which we know are not safe," Samuelsson told reporters. The technology, which Volvo ultimately expects to support hands-free driving both in urban environments and on highways, should appear in Volvo vehicles before 2030 and will be launched in multiple regions simultaneously, excluding China, Alwin Bakkenes, Volvo Cars' head of software engineering, said. Volvo, majority-owned by China's Geely Holding (GEELY.UL), has not chosen a pricing model yet, Bakkenes said, but features would not be limited to higher-priced models.

item.title: Haas signs Rafael Camara to F1 seat to replace Esteban Ocon
item.description: Haas has signed 21-year-old Formula 2 driver Rafael Camara to fill its vacant Formula 1 seat starting in 2027.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Haas has signed 21-year-old Formula 2 driver Rafael Camara to fill its vacant Formula 1 seat starting in 2027. The Brazilian driver will replace Esteban Ocon, who announced last month that he is leaving Haas after two seasons. Camara, who currently leads the F2 standings as a rookie, secured a multi-year deal to make his F1 debut with Haas. Haas conducted tests with reserve drivers Ryo Hirakawa and Jack Doohan and reigning F2 champ Leonardo Fornaroli. Camara became the leading target, however, following a private test with Haas in August at Portimao in Portugal. "He showed when we had him drive in our (test) program in Portugal that he could handle himself very well with not a huge amount of time to learn the car," Ayao Komatsu, Haas F1 team principal, said in a statement. "He showed us more than just raw speed. Rafa managed to create an environment to get the best out of himself, it was very impressive and certainly the laps he completed were special." Camara, who joined the Ferrari Driver Academy in 2022, won the Formula 3 title in 2025 driving for Trident. He is driving for Invicta Racing this season and has recorded three wins and five pole positions. He leads the F2 standings by seven points with two races remaining. --Field Level Media

item.title: IEA to speed up oil stocks release including over 20 million barrels of diesel
item.description: The International Energy Agency agreed on Thursday to release over 20 million barrels of diesel to the market and any oil remaining from a record emergency reserves release pledged in March to boost supply and cool soaring prices.
item.dc:creator: Forrest Crellin, Robert Harvey, Pietro Lombardi
item.content:encoded: The International Energy Agency agreed on Thursday to release over 20 million barrels of diesel to the market and any oil remaining from a record emergency reserves release pledged in March to boost supply and cool soaring prices. US President Donald Trump has pressed European Union countries to draw down reserves or face a potential US diesel export ban as he seeks to lower prices ahead of November 3 [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterm elections"]. Diesel prices have surged to record highs in many markets due to disrupted supply because of the Iran war and the Russia-Ukraine conflict, posing inflation and cost-of-living threats to governments and consumers. The 32-nation IEA's board met on Thursday to discuss the scale and timing of stock releases. "The IEA governing board reaffirmed its commitment to continue delivering on the March 2026 Collective Action in response to the Strait of Hormuz crisis," it said in a statement after the meeting. In March, countries had pledged to release more than 400 million barrels of crude and oil products as prices soared. On Thursday, members "agreed to accelerate the release of the remaining volumes, with specific plans already in place, including over 20 million barrels of diesel as soon as possible." SOME DISAPPOINTMENT OVER LACK OF EXTRA BARRELS Reuters reported this month that EU governments were discussing a [USN:S8N43A07P TEXT:"French proposal"] for the release of 50 million barrels of diesel alongside 50 million barrels of crude from IEA members. "The IEA announcement is a step in the right direction, but falls short on the details the market was looking for," said Abhishek Kumar, an analyst at Sparta Commodities. "The 20+ million barrels of diesel appear to be an acceleration of existing commitments rather than genuinely new volumes." The IEA, which coordinates industrialised nations' releases of oil from emergency stocks, said some members had already released more than they pledged in March and that others planned to do so. Members have released approximately 330 million barrels so far, the IEA said. The US Energy Department said further IEA releases, with a focus on diesel, are under review and in progress, citing the IEA statement. But the Trump administration "continues to hold European nations accountable for failing to fulfill their previous commitments to minimize supply disruptions in global energy markets and to help lower energy prices," the Energy Department spokesperson added. The White House, when asked if it was unhappy with the IEA's commitment to draw down reserves, provided the IEA's statement from Thursday on the releases. Spain [USN:L8N4610R5 TEXT:"said on Thursday"] it would release 4.4 million barrels from strategic reserves in October. Spain has released 3.7 million of the 11.5 million barrels it pledged in March.

item.title: FBI, US Postal Service investigate suspicious mailings to election officials, lawmakers
item.description: The FBI and US Postal Service's law enforcement arm said on Thursday they were investigating suspicious mailings, including some sent to state election officials and lawmakers' offices ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: The FBI and US Postal Service's law enforcement arm said on Thursday they were investigating suspicious mailings, including some sent to state election officials and lawmakers' offices ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. The FBI said some of the letters contained an unknown substance. The investigation come less than three weeks before the midterms, which will determine control of the US Congress, as the Postal Service prepares to handle millions of mailed ballots. Spokespeople for Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer, Alex Padilla, a California Democrat, and Chris Murphy, a Connecticut Democrat, all said the US Postal Service intercepted letters containing a suspicious substance mailed to their offices. "This incident is a stark reminder of the very real dangers facing those who serve the public and who help administer our elections," Padilla said in a statement. The US House of Representatives sergeant at arms, the House's chief law enforcement officer, told staff in an email seen by Reuters that some public officials had received letters containing suspicious white powder substances. Brendan Donahue, a deputy chief inspector with the US Postal Inspection Service, said some suspicious letters had been intercepted and that an investigation was ongoing. "We are committed to protecting our nation's election officials from threatening and dangerous mail. Any threat or attack on an election official is unacceptable," Donahue told reporters. The National Association of Secretaries of State and the National Association of State Election Directors said late on Wednesday a series of suspicious letters was sent to state election offices. Letters bound for several state election offices were intercepted before they were delivered, including in Pennsylvania, Ohio and Idaho. The Wisconsin Elections Commission said on Thursday it received a suspicious letter with an unidentified powdery substance that was deemed not hazardous. "Let this be very clear: this incident will not shake us,” said Meagan Wolfe, the state’s chief election official. An email to Senate staff said suspicious letters could have postmarks that do not match the return address and included an image of an envelope with a return address labeled "DSA" and a New York City address. POSTAL SERVICE PLANS NEW MEASURES Earlier on Thursday, US Postmaster General David Steiner said USPS was "absolutely ready" to handle millions of ballots for the midterm elections. USPS said this month it would take "extraordinary measures" for the 2026 election, including extending hours at some retail locations and expediting handling, extra deliveries and special pickups of ballots. On September 14, the US Supreme Court declined to let USPS enforce a rule targeting mail-in ballots, dealing a setback to President Donald Trump's effort to restrict voting by mail. USPS said it would not enforce the rule under the order. The agency adopted the measure after Trump issued a March executive order aimed at tightening rules governing mail voting. In 2024, USPS delivered 99.2 million ballots to and from voters in the presidential election. About 30% of votes were cast by mail in the November 2024 presidential election, down from 46% in 2020. Trump's fellow Republicans are locked in a tight battle to retain control of Congress in the midterms. Democratic voters disproportionately use mail-in ballots, according to various surveys, so restricting them could benefit Republicans. Under the rule that was blocked, states would have had to provide lists of mail-ballot recipients to USPS and use agency-approved outbound and return ballot mail envelopes outfitted with unique barcodes. The Postal Service could then have refused to send out ballots that did not comply or were associated with voters not appearing on the lists.

item.title: US delays small imports rule that raised alarm over prescription drug costs
item.description: The US government has delayed by 90 days implementation of new customs requirements for small international mail shipments, a move that should forestall higher prices for imported prescription drugs and other products for inflation-weary Americans until after the November midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Kamal Choudhury
item.content:encoded: The US government has delayed by 90 days implementation of new customs requirements for small international mail shipments, a move that should forestall higher prices for imported prescription drugs and other products for inflation-weary Americans until after the November midterm elections . The US Customs and Border Protection rule targets the [USN:L1N44A13F TEXT:"de minimis tariffs exemption"], which has eased requirements for shipments under $800. The rule aimed to speed up implementation of changes authorized by US lawmakers as part of President Donald Trump's spending and tax-cut bill, which are due to take effect in July 2027. The agency said on Wednesday it has pushed the mandatory compliance date for a new mail entry process to January 20, 2027, from October 22. That prior deadline was just 12 days before the November 3 elections in which US households' affordability woes are a central issue dogging Trump's Republican Party with control of Congress up for grabs. It said there would be no changes to international mail entry procedures before then. The process requires electronic filing for postal shipments subject to Section 201, 232 or 301 duties, or under the jurisdiction of a partner government agency such as the US Food and Drug Administration. It also involves a customs bond. As the October 22 deadline approached, patient advocates and industry groups had warned the rule's data and bonding requirements could cause delays, refusals or added costs for personal drug orders. IMPACT ON PHARMA The FDA officially bars individuals from importing foreign prescription drugs, but it has discretion in limited circumstances. Some Americans order medicines from other countries like Canada, where the cost of drugs can be sharply lower. The Canadian International Pharmacy Association has said most routine personal orders from licensed foreign pharmacies could be disrupted. A separate letter signed by 71 members of Congress, led by Democratic Representatives Jan Schakowsky of Illinois and Wisconsin's Mark Pocan, asked agencies to delay the procedures for prescription medicines unless personal-use drugs were assured. “For patients concerned about losing access to lower-cost prescriptions from abroad, this delay is a welcome reprieve, but not a permanent solution," said Merith Basey, CEO of Patients For Affordable Drugs. "Until patients in the US can get access to the prescription drugs they need at prices they can afford, disrupting existing personal-importation practices risks an important safety valve.” The Department of Health and Human Services referred questions to CBP, which did not immediately respond to a request for comment on whether personal-use exemptions are planned. CBP said the extension gives importers, brokers and logistics providers more time to update processes, helps avoid disruptions and will close gaps that have been exploited by smugglers. CBP's announcement did not mention medicines, and the rule does not name them.

item.title: Italian holding company Delfin explores funding for potential internal stake buyout, sources say
item.description: Delfin, the holding company of Italy's Del Vecchio family and top shareholder in EssilorLuxottica , has held preliminary talks with banks to explore financing options for a possible purchase of stakes in Delfin held by one or more shareholders, two people close to the matter said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Delfin, the holding company of Italy's Del Vecchio family and top shareholder in EssilorLuxottica (ESLX.PA) , has held preliminary talks with banks to explore financing options for a possible purchase of stakes in Delfin held by one or more shareholders, two people close to the matter said on Thursday. Disagreements among the eight heirs of late EssilorLuxottica founder Leonardo Del Vecchio have left Delfin in a prolonged deadlock, preventing the family from ending a succession dispute and acting cohesively to influence decisions at the holding company. The discussions on taking over stakes are at a very early stage and there is no certainty they will lead to a transaction, the people added. Delfin declined to comment. Italy's Corriere della Sera reported on Thursday that Delfin was exploring the acquisition of two shareholders' stakes, equivalent to about 25% of the company. It did not identify the two shareholders. Such a deal would reduce the number of heirs holding shares in Delfin from eight to six, leaving each with an interest of roughly 16.5% instead of 12.5%. Delfin has a net asset value estimated at around €40 billion ($44.87 billion), with the bulk of it coming from the 32.4% stake in EssilorLuxottica. It also has minority stakes in Italian bank MPS (BMPS.MI) and insurer Assicurazioni Generali (GASI.MI) among others. In the first half of this year, Leonardo Maria Del Vecchio sought to buy out two of his siblings, offering around €10 billion for a combined 25% stake in Delfin, but the deal [USN:L1N4320JW TEXT:"did not materialise"]. At that time, EssilorLuxottica CEO Francesco Milleri, who is also Delfin chair, [USN:S8N3YM04U TEXT:"welcomed"] a streamlined Delfin ownership structure. Italian daily Il Sole 24 Ore reported on Thursday that discussions were focused on a possible acquisition by Delfin of the 12.5% stake held by Leonardo Maria Del Vecchio, who earlier this week renewed criticism of Chief Executive Francesco Milleri's leadership of EssilorLuxottica.
