item.title: El S&P 500 cierra en alza; los inversores se pasan de la inteligencia artificial al sector de salud
item.description: El S&P 500 cerró con un alza el jueves, recuperándose de pérdidas iniciales, ya que los inversores, preocupados por las acciones del sector de la inteligencia artificial (IA), se decantaron por Eli Lilly, UnitedHealth y otras de los sectores de salud y de consumo.
item.dc:creator: Noel Randewich, Sruthi Shankar
item.content:encoded: El S&P 500 cerró con un alza el jueves, recuperándose de pérdidas iniciales, ya que los inversores, preocupados por las acciones del sector de la inteligencia artificial (IA), se decantaron por Eli Lilly, UnitedHealth y otras de los sectores de salud y de consumo. Varias acciones tecnológicas cayeron, ya que los inversores analizaron con detenimiento las empresas relacionadas con la inteligencia artificial, cuyo alto endeudamiento las hace vulnerables a las subidas de las tasas de interés. Las acciones de Eli Lilly (LLY.N) , UnitedHealth (UNH.N) y Walmart repuntaron después de que Deutsche Bank revisó al alza sus recomendaciones. Broadcom (AVGO.O) y Nvidia (NVDA.O) bajaron después de que el fabricante de chips TSMC (2330.TW) se mostró cauto sobre 2027, a pesar de reportar por sexto trimestre consecutivo una ganancia récord gracias a la sólida demanda impulsada por la inteligencia artificial. Dell Technologies (DELL.N) y Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE.N) profundizaron las fuertes pérdidas de la sesión anterior, debido a la preocupación por las empresas de IA expuestas a unos costos de financiamiento más altos. El rendimiento de los bonos del Tesoro a 10 años retrocedió, pero se mantuvo cerca de máximos de varios años, ya que a los inversores les preocupa la inflación relacionada con los altos precios del petróleo. "El costo de financiar cualquier cosa, ya sea una nueva vivienda unifamiliar o un gigantesco centro de datos, está aumentando, y eso tiene implicaciones para muchos aspectos del mercado bursátil", dijo Jed Ellerbroek, gestor de carteras de Argent Capital Management. "Las acciones con mejor rendimiento hoy son las de empresas defensivas y no cíclicas". El índice de semiconductores de Filadelfia (.SOX) cayó por séptima sesión consecutiva. Según datos preliminares, el S&P 500 (.SPX) subió 24,94 puntos, un 0,32%, a 7.744,07 unidades; el Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) ganó 18,37 puntos, un 0,07%, a 26.711,24 unidades; el Promedio Industrial Dow Jones (.DJI) sumó 559,45 puntos, o un 1,08%, a 52.180,93 unidades.

item.title: Yemen's Houthis hit palace in Aden, coalition details attacks on Saudi infrastructure
item.description: Yemen's Houthis fired missiles at the presidential palace complex in the southern city of Aden on Thursday, killing five people, the government said, as the Saudi-led coalition listed dozens of Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure in recent weeks.
item.dc:creator: Enas Alashray, Mohammed Ghobari, Eman Abouhassira
item.content:encoded: Yemen's Houthis fired missiles at the presidential palace complex in the southern city of Aden on Thursday, killing five people, the government said, as the Saudi-led coalition listed dozens of Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure in recent weeks. The attack was the first in the current conflict between the Iran-aligned Houthis and Saudi Arabia on Aden's Al-Maashiq palace, the seat of Yemen's Saudi-backed and internationally recognised government. The conflict is a new theatre in the wider regional war that began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran in February. Yemen's prime minister and cabinet members were safe following the attack, Yemeni Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani said. Witnesses told Reuters they heard loud booms near the palace. Yemen's cabinet said the attack involved missiles and drones. Yemen's health minister Qasim Buhaibeh said five people were killed and 16 wounded in what he described as a Houthi attack on the government's official headquarters at the presidential complex. The casualties included guards and civilian employees. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said its fighters had bombed what he described as the Saudi military operations headquarters in Aden, as part of the group's declared policy of targeting "Saudi reinforcements wherever they were located". The Houthi-run news agency SABA said the headquarters was run by Saudi officers and that there were weapons depots there. Reuters could not independently verify the claims. Fighting between the Houthis and Saudi-backed forces resumed last month, and aid agencies [USN:L6N4600ML TEXT:"have warned"] of rapidly worsening conditions in Yemen. Last week, government forces launched a campaign to recapture areas controlled by the Houthis, recovering ground near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key shipping artery. War broke out in Yemen in 2014 when [USN:L1N45Q02Z TEXT:"the Houthis"] seized the capital Sanaa, driving the government south. A Saudi-led military intervention the following year led to a bloody stalemate before a 2022 truce that held until this year. In that phase of the conflict Houthi fighters and allied forces briefly seized Al-Maashiq palace during a battle for Aden, before withdrawing. COALITION SAYS HOUTHIS ARE GETTING MISSILES, FAST BOATS As Saudi Arabia backs government forces, the Houthis [USN:L1N4610L5 TEXT:"have been firing"] ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi airports, ports and oil installations, turning US ally Saudi Arabia into a [USN:L1N46108L TEXT:"pressure point"] in the wider war [USN:L6N45Y0GN TEXT:"and threatening"] its ambitious economic plans. On Thursday, the Saudi-led military coalition said the Houthis had attempted to attack dozens of such sites, highlighting the risk to Saudi civilian infrastructure. The governing council of the UN's International Civil Aviation Organization condemned the recent attacks on civilian airports, aircraft, and aviation infrastructure in Saudi Arabia. Coalition spokesperson Turki al-Maliki told reporters that the Houthis had launched 20 attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh this month, killing 17 people and wounding 333 others. The airport is one of Saudi Arabia's main international aviation hubs. The coalition said Houthi attacks on Abha airport in southwestern Saudi Arabia near the Yemeni border had killed three people and wounded 28. Maliki said the Houthis had acquired advanced military technology with the help of "regional actors," including ballistic missiles, drones and explosive-laden fast boats. Iran [USN:L1N43P0D6 TEXT:"has provided"] weapons, money and training to the Houthis, although Tehran has officially denied arming them in violation of a UN arms embargo. Maliki also said the coalition had destroyed 127 weapons storage facilities and launch platforms in Yemen's mountainous areas, calling on the Houthis to immediately halt operations targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure. Shortly afterwards, the Houthi military spokesperson said Saudi airspace and airports were unsafe, renewing a warning to airlines while excluding airspace over the holy cities of Mecca and Medina. Saudi Arabia's civil defence authority issued early-warning alerts throughout Thursday over potential threats in the cities of Najran and Jizan, as well as the wider Najran and Jazan regions, before later saying the danger had passed. The Saudi-led coalition said on Thursday that it had intercepted and destroyed a drone in the southwestern Saudi Arabian city of Khamis Mushait, and another launched towards the country's southern region.

item.title: Hurricane Trudy looms over Mexico's Pacific coast, severe rainfall expected
item.description: Hurricane Trudy moved parallel to Mexico's western coast on Thursday, threatening further rain and strong winds in a region already battered in recent weeks by storms that left behind several deaths and severe flooding.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Hurricane Trudy moved parallel to Mexico's western coast on Thursday, threatening further rain and strong winds in a region already battered in recent weeks by storms that left behind several deaths and severe flooding. The storm, located about 480 km (298 miles) south-southwest of beach town Acapulco, packed maximum sustained winds of 120 kph (75 mph) and is moving northwest, the US-based National Hurricane Center said in a morning advisory. • Trudy, a Category 1 hurricane, is forecast to rapidly intensify into a major hurricane on Friday. • The storm is then expected to approach Mexico's Pacific coast with heavy rains forecast in the states of Colima and Jalisco, increasing the risk of life-threatening flooding and landslides, the NHC and Mexican authorities warned. • Meanwhile, Tropical Storm Simon is nearly stationary farther northwest offshore, after [USN:L1N45Y0H6 TEXT:"dropping heavy rain"] along the coast earlier as a hurricane. • Simon is forecast to move northwest, grazing the Baja California peninsula over the weekend, the NHC added.

item.title: Nvidia, Apple each gave $25 million for Trump's ballroom, Washington Post reports
item.description: Nvidia and Apple each committed $25 million for US President Donald Trump's planned White House ballroom, according to a Washington Post report on Thursday that showed $333 million in private donations for the project.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Nvidia (NVDA.O) and Apple (AAPL.O) each committed $25 million for US President Donald Trump's planned White House ballroom, according to a Washington Post report on Thursday that showed $333 million in private donations for the project. The Adelson family, longtime financial supporters of Trump and his Republican Party, committed $25 million as well, as did billionaire Charles Ergen, co-founder and chairman of telecommunications company Dish Network, the report added. The president himself is not on the list, according to the Post. Reuters has not verified the report. The White House said it would not release information about the donors, who spokesman Davis Ingle said "represent a wide array of great American companies." "The same critics who are alleging fake conflicts of interests would also complain if American taxpayers were footing the bill for these long-overdue renovations," Ingle told Reuters. Nvidia said it was proud to make a donation to a nonpartisan trust that serves Americans. "As an American company, our support for the United States is paramount, and independent of any business interests," a spokesperson said. Apple declined to comment. The scale of the ballroom project and the administration’s handling of fundraising and disclosures have drawn criticism from watchdog groups and legal experts, who say they raise questions about transparency, donor influence and adherence to longstanding ethics and oversight norms. "The secrecy is a huge problem," said Eric Petry of the Brennan Center for Justice. "When people with business before the government can give millions to the president's pet project, and the public can't see who or how much, there's no way to tell whether they're buying access or favors." Federal contractors including Lockheed Martin Corp, Microsoft Corp and Palantir Technologies Inc all gave $10 million, the Post reported. The companies did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Trump initially said he and wealthy donors would pay for the estimated $400 million project, but he later unsuccessfully sought $1 billion from Congress for an underground bunker and security features to harden the facility. The Post reported that the "vast majority of the funds raised came from companies and wealthy individuals with interests before the federal government" and that half the total came from companies or executives of firms that have had federal government contracts in Trump's second White House term. The planned ballroom is among [USN:L1N3YZ1G0 TEXT:"several projects"] Trump is pursuing in his efforts to remake Washington with sweeping, unilateral changes that his opponents have challenged in court and called a power grab. The US Supreme Court, in a 5-4 [USN:S0N42U037 TEXT:"ruling"] in August, allowed Trump to continue construction of the ballroom while he challenges a judicial order that would halt much of the development. In a dissent, Chief Justice John Roberts said the project was "likely unlawful." The ballroom, which Trump has said will seat 1,000 guests, has faced public backlash. Preservationists and opponents say Trump exceeded his authority by demolishing the historic East Wing, which housed the first lady's offices and the White House movie theater, to make room for the structure. Trump says a planned 90,000-square-foot (8,360-square-meter) White House ballroom will include bomb shelters, medical facilities, defenses against drones and missiles and other security features. Confronted with criticism of the project, his administration now says the facility is needed for national security, an argument the president has also made about a proposed triumphal arch.

item.title: Huracán Trudy se intensifica frente a costa del Pacífico mexicano
item.description: El huracán Trudy se intensificaba rápidamente sobre el océano Pacífico, a medida que se acercaba a la costa occidental de México, amenazando con dejar más lluvias y fuertes vientos en una zona castigada en las últimas semanas por varios ciclones tropicales que han causado inundaciones y algunos muertos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El huracán Trudy se intensificaba rápidamente sobre el océano Pacífico, a medida que se acercaba a la costa occidental de México, amenazando con dejar más lluvias y fuertes vientos en una zona castigada en las últimas semanas por varios ciclones tropicales que han causado inundaciones y algunos muertos. A las 11.00 hora local (1700 GMT), el ciclón se ubicaba a unos 430 kilómetros al sur-suroeste del puerto Acapulco, en el estado Guerrero, y soplaba vientos máximos sostenidos de 150 kilómetros por hora (km/h), con ráfagas más fuertes, mientras avanzaba hacia el norte-noroeste a 9 km/h, según datos del Centro Nacional de Huracanes de Estados Unidos (NHC, por su sigla en inglés). Se espera que Trudy se siga intensificando hasta convertirse en un huracán de categoría 4 en la escala de Saffir-Simpson. Un ciclón de ese nivel puede soplar vientos máximos sostenidos de hasta 250 km/h y causar daños generalizados en estructuras protectoras, desplome de tejados en edificios pequeños, erosión de bancales y playas e inundaciones en terrenos interiores. "Si Trudy se intensifica como se pronostica, los fuertes vientos cerca de su centro generarán olas peligrosamente altas en alta mar. El oleaje se extenderá hacia afuera, amenazando tanto a embarcaciones pequeñas como a grandes buques", advirtió AccuWeather, una compañía estadounidense de servicios comerciales de pronóstico del tiempo. Si bien no se prevé que Trudy toque tierra, descargaría fuertes lluvias en la franja costera que va desde el conocido destino turístico Acapulco hasta Puerto Vallarta, pasando por los dos mayores puertos del país; Lázaro Cárdenas y Manzanillo. En las últimas semanas, la misma zona ya fue golpeada por los huracanes [USN:L6N45L0YK TEXT:"Polo"] y [USN:L8N45V0SM TEXT:"Simón"]. Si bien este último tampoco tocó tierra, sigue activo, aunque como tormenta tropical, frente a la costa del Pacífico mexicano.

item.title: CCC Intelligent Solutions agrees to $6.1 billion take-private deal with GTCR, Elliott
item.description: CCC Intelligent Solutions said on Thursday it agreed to be acquired by a consortium of private investment firms led by GTCR and including Elliott Investment Management in a $6.1 billion take-private deal.
item.dc:creator: Milana Vinn
item.content:encoded: CCC Intelligent Solutions (CCC.O) said on Thursday it agreed to be acquired by a consortium of private investment firms led by GTCR and including Elliott Investment Management in a $6.1 billion take-private deal. Shareholders of the Chicago-based company will receive $7.75 in cash for each share held, CCC said. The offer represents a 44% premium to the stock's close on July 9, before [USN:L6N43B182 TEXT:"Reuters reported the company was exploring a sale"]. CCC provides software to the property and casualty insurance industry, including tools for claims management and damage estimation. Software valuations are under pressure amid concerns that artificial intelligence could disrupt businesses, slow growth and erode earnings. Investors have been largely indiscriminate in their selloff of software stocks, creating opportunities for private equity firms to acquire companies they view as undervalued, said Nelson Iginla, a principal at GTCR. "CCC is a business where the stock price was much higher historically ... but as we look at the actual underlying performance of the business, the performance has been extremely strong," Iginla said. "When you peel things back, it's a business that we think is made better by AI, not worse by AI." Earlier this year, the company faced investor concerns over slowing growth, softer claims volumes and a slower-than-expected rollout of some newer software products, which had weighed on its share price. The company said the deal followed a review of strategic options. Private equity firm Advent International acquired CCC in 2017. Advent later took the company public through a merger with a blank-check company in 2021 and exited its investment in 2025. The deal is not subject to financing conditions and is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, after which CCC will become privately held. The company is scheduled to report third-quarter results on October 29. CCC shares were little changed at $7.61 in Thursday trading, after rising recently on media reports of a potential deal. Morgan Stanley is advising CCC, while J.P. Morgan and Citi are advising GTCR. Simpson Thacher & Bartlett served as legal counsel to GTCR, and Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher and Debevoise & Plimpton served as legal counsel to Elliott.

item.title: Dólar cae desde máximo de 18 meses porque alza de bonos modera preocupación por la inflación
item.description: El dólar retrocedió el jueves desde un máximo de 18 meses, porque los inversores miraron más allá de los sólidos datos de inflación y gasto en Estados Unidos para centrarse en la caída de los valores de las empresas de centros de datos de inteligencia artificial.
item.dc:creator: Laura Matthews
item.content:encoded: El dólar retrocedió el jueves desde un máximo de 18 meses, porque los inversores miraron más allá de los sólidos datos de inflación y gasto en Estados Unidos para centrarse en la caída de los valores de las empresas de centros de datos de inteligencia artificial. * Los precios al productor en Estados Unidos registraron en septiembre su mayor aumento en cuatro años y medio debido al alza en los costos de bienes y servicios, lo que refuerza la evidencia de que las presiones inflacionarias se están extendiendo a otros sectores desde el energético. * Las ventas minoristas aumentaron más de lo previsto, impulsadas por los precios más altos de la gasolina, mientras que las solicitudes semanales de subsidio por desempleo subieron levemente, apuntando a una demanda de los consumidores resiliente y a un mercado laboral estable. * Sin embargo, el precio de los bonos gubernamentales repuntó y el dólar retrocedió, reflejando comentarios cautos de autoridades monetarias de la Reserva Federal que enfriaron aún más las expectativas de un alza de las tasas de interés en octubre. * "Tenemos una narrativa negativa para el dólar basada en la idea de que la inflación a este nivel y a este ritmo acelerado es insostenible", dijo Juan Pérez, director de operaciones de Monex USA en Washington. * "A pesar de las malas noticias en el frente de guerra y del panorama bursátil pesimista, el mercado se muestra contrario al dólar tras un fuerte repunte en las últimas cuatro semanas (...) El estancamiento económico parece estar influyendo cada vez más en la opinión de los operadores", agregó. * El índice dólar , que compara al billete verde con una cesta de seis destacadas divisas, cayó un 0,45%, a 101,99 unidades, tras haber alcanzado el miércoles un máximo en 18 meses después de que las cifras de inflación en Estados Unidos resultaron más altas de lo esperado. * El euro repuntó un 0,56% desde un mínimo de 18 meses, a 1,1218 dólares, para su mayor avance diario en casi dos meses. La libra esterlina ganó un 0,64%, a 1,3275 dólares, tras datos que mostraron que la economía británica creció un 0,1% en agosto. * El yen se fortaleció un 0,15%, a 158,08 unidades por dólar.

item.title: TSX rises, touches three-week high
item.description: Canada's main stock index closed higher on Thursday, touching a three-week high, powered by mining and tech stocks as lower bond yields boosted risk appetite, offsetting weakness in energy shares.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Canada's main stock index closed higher on Thursday, touching a three-week high, powered by mining and tech stocks as lower bond yields boosted risk appetite, offsetting weakness in energy shares. The S&P/TSX Composite Index (.GSPTSE) was up 1.55%, at 36,137.10, rebounding after sharp declines in the previous session. Canada's benchmark 10-year bond yield slipped to 3.828%, driving broad sectoral gains. Materials sector (.GSPTTMT) , including metal miners, gained 3.3% as precious metal prices rebounded on a softer dollar. The S&P 500 ended higher, springing back from early losses as investors concerned about AI stocks shifted into Eli Lilly, UnitedHealth and other healthcare and consumer stocks. Canadian tech equities (.SPTTTK) gained 2.3%, with e-commerce platform Shopify (SHOP.TO) gaining 2.9%. Energy sector (.SPTTEN) slipped 0.5% as investors weighed possible US steps to ease restrictions on the world’s "shadow fleet" of tankers, while conflict in the Middle East kept a geopolitical risk premium in the market. Canadian [USN:AQN2MO654 TEXT:"factory sales"] grew 1.5% in August from July on higher sales of primary metals, data showed on Thursday. Still, economists remain cautious about recovery in manufacturing considering limited sectoral gains. "This reinforces our view that the Bank of Canada will deliver only two of the roughly four rate hikes currently priced in by markets, with tightening serving more as a risk-management exercise against upside inflation risks," said Thomas Ryan, senior North America economist, Capital Economics.

item.title: Israeli firm used online ads to run vast spy operation, researchers say
item.description: Israeli digital advertising agency Discover-Tech spied on internet users through a sprawling network of online ads that it used to track targets and help hack their devices, two research groups said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Raphael Satter
item.content:encoded: Israeli digital advertising agency Discover-Tech spied on internet users through a sprawling network of online ads that it used to track targets and help hack their devices, two research groups said on Thursday. Its services gave Israel's Candiru — a spyware company [USN:L1N2RU186 TEXT:"blacklisted by the US government"] — as well as other Israeli surveillance firms access to advertising platforms run by Google (GOOGL.O) , Comcast (CMCSA.O) , Russia's Yandex and others, according to separate reports from Canadian cyber watchdog group Citizen Lab and New York advertising security firm Confiant. The reports show how the online advertising business, long a subject of privacy concerns, can also serve as a channel for sweeping espionage campaigns. "The way online advertising works today is a systemic security threat," Wolfie Christl, a senior researcher at Citizen Lab, told Reuters. "For states, the private sector, civil society and everyone else alike." Discover-Tech's online ads — often for ordinary products such as phones or earbuds — reached more than 120,000 websites and 75,000 apps through its various partnerships, Citizen Lab said. Users who visited sites or used apps with the malicious ads could be identified and tracked by Discover-Tech, which would sometimes also try to extract phone numbers from some smartphone users, the researchers said. Ads only needed to load on a website for the spying to occur. Some ads would be used to help plant spyware from Candiru on users' devices, both research groups said, though Confiant said that ads it tied to Candiru were a tiny fraction of Discover-Tech's overall volume. MALICIOUS ADS SHOWN IN HUNDREDS OF SENSITIVE NETWORKS Confiant cofounder Jerome Dangu said Discover-Tech was pumping out at least 10 million ads per day all around the world and that data-sharing arrangements — called cookie matching — allowed it to track people even beyond the reach of its advertisements. "Very likely hundreds of millions of people would have been touched by Discover-Tech," Dangu said. Discover-Tech, which was founded in 2020, did not return messages left via its contact form. A LinkedIn message and emails sent to its chief executive, Dekel Boni, were not returned. Reuters' attempts to reach Candiru's owners were similarly unsuccessful. The US Commerce Department blacklisted Candiru in 2021 for [USN:L1N2RU186 TEXT:"allegedly supplying spyware"] that was used to maliciously target government officials, journalists, activists and academics. Citizen Lab said a powerful form of Candiru spyware delivered through Discover-Tech's ads had been used to compromise 45 Windows devices at the Qatari broadcaster Al Jazeera between 2024 and 2025, something it said it was able to confirm because the media group had shared its network logs with the group. In a statement, Al Jazeera said it "condemns the spyware attacks targeting a number of its staff" and that it was taking steps to protect its employees and its systems. "Those responsible must be held accountable," it said. Dangu of Confiant said that the malicious ads had been shown to users in "hundreds of networks in sensitive categories," including the Pentagon, the International Atomic Energy Agency, and the International Criminal Court. He also said that some regions, like the Palestinian territories, were particularly saturated by the Israeli firm's ads. "You go to almost any site in Palestine — any site — you find a Discover-Tech ad. It gives them a very complete visibility on the digital activities of an entire country," he said. Citizen Lab also said it had similar evidence showing the malicious ads were shown to people in the United Nations, NATO, the European Commission, and more than a dozen national governments. Other networks the ads appeared in included chip-related firms such as Nvidia (NVDA.O) , Sandisk (SNDK.O) , Broadcom (AVGO.O) , and Micron (MU.O) , as well as several media organizations in Mexico, Israel, and Europe that were not identified. In addition to identifying Candiru and a couple of other surveillance vendors, Citizen Lab said it was able to glean some details about where Discover-Tech's users might be based because the firm inadvertently exposed its authentication logs to the internet, showing people logging in from internet protocol addresses in Israel, Europe, and the Gulf. MEASURES AGAINST DISCOVER-TECH TAKEN Discover-Tech is now being frozen out of parts of the online ad market. Google said in a statement that it had collaborated with Citizen Lab and Confiant's investigation and kicked Discover-Tech off its ad platforms "for systematically violating our policies." IAB Europe, the European-level association for the digital marketing and advertising ecosystem, said in an email that Discover-Tech had been suspended from its list of globally approved vendors last week after an audit identified policy violations. Comcast ad tech subsidiary Beeswax removed Discover-Tech from its platform "following recent activity," Comcast said in a statement. Yandex did not return Reuters messages seeking comment. Advertising-driven surveillance is increasingly being seen as a national security threat. Earlier this year, the Pentagon said it had received reports that US forces deployed to war zones had been [USN:L6N4240BC TEXT:"targeted using location data"] harvested by ad tech firms and data brokers. Branches of the military have since [USN:L6N44V02G TEXT:"disabled ad tracking"] on some devices.

item.title: AstraZeneca strikes $40 million AI drug discovery deal with insitro
item.description: AstraZeneca has teamed up with artificial intelligence biotech company insitro to discover and develop new treatments for difficult to treat liver and heart conditions, the British drugmaker said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Wingrove
item.content:encoded: AstraZeneca (AZN.L) has teamed up with artificial intelligence biotech company insitro to discover and develop new treatments for difficult to treat liver and heart conditions, the British drugmaker said on Thursday. Under the agreement, AstraZeneca will pay $40 million up front, with California-based insitro eligible for up to about $1.46 billion in potential development and commercial milestones, as well as a single-digit percentage of future sales in royalties. The multi-year collaboration will focus on metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), a severe liver disease, and cardiomyopathies, a group of diseases that affect the heart muscle. Both have historically lacked effective therapies because researchers have struggled to pinpoint their root biological drivers, the drugmaker said. Insitro will use its "Virtual Human" AI platform, which combines lab-grown cell models and machine learning, to identify causal disease biology and advance AstraZeneca-nominated targets from discovery to development-candidate stage. AstraZeneca will then run and fund future clinical trials. The deal builds on insitro's expansion across the pharmaceuticals industry. The biotech company recently expanded its partnership with Bristol Myers Squibb (BMY.N) to advance a broader portfolio of targets for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). It also teamed up with Eli Lilly (LLY.N) to build AI models that predict pharmacological properties of small molecules in living organisms. "Choosing the new targets that we want to put into our discovery pipeline is one of the hardest things we do across research and development," Sharon Barr, executive vice president of biopharmaceuticals R&D at AstraZeneca, told Reuters. "By the time we read about a new pathway or target (in major scientific journals), it is no longer novel. It's in the public domain and we're already a few steps too late. But when we identify these unique connections early and test them in cellular systems, we're ahead of the game." Barr added that pairing AI tools with experienced scientists allows the company to test fewer molecules in the lab, reduce guesswork and speed the search for effective medicines.

item.title: Cohere moves to buy AI cybersecurity startup Aisle
item.description: Canadian AI lab Cohere said on Thursday it had signed a letter of intent to buy Aisle, a San Francisco-based cybersecurity startup that uses AI to detect vulnerabilities in software.
item.dc:creator: Leo Marchandon
item.content:encoded: Canadian AI lab Cohere said on Thursday it had signed a letter of intent to buy Aisle, a San Francisco-based cybersecurity startup that uses AI to detect vulnerabilities in software. The terms of the deal were not disclosed. The tie-up would add cybersecurity to the business entity Cohere is assembling through its [USN:L6N4580NZ TEXT:"merger with Germany's Aleph Alpha"], a combination reported to be worth about $20 billion. It would also extend its European footprint with Aisle's engineering hub in Prague. Cohere said the acquisition reflected its continued investment in Europe and would deepen its presence across the region, strengthening European AI. The deal is aimed at boosting the combined group's security and threat detection capabilities for enterprise and public sector clients, with private deployment available on the customer's own system. "Increasingly capable AI systems are transforming both cybersecurity and the threats organizations face, and defensive capabilities must advance just as quickly," Cohere said. Aisle was founded in 2025 by Ondrej Vlcek, former CEO of Czech antivirus maker Avast, with co-founders from Google (GOOGL.O) DeepMind and Anthropic. Vlcek will join Cohere to lead its new cybersecurity unit, while Aisle Chief Operating Officer Jaya Baloo will become its chief information security officer and Aisle's 50 full-time employees will join Cohere, the Canadian company told Reuters. Aisle said its AI found more than 500 new bugs in widely used software in its first year, including 12 vulnerabilities in OpenSSL, a free program that encrypts internet traffic for banks, governments and messaging apps. The bugs were fixed after their discovery.

item.title: S&P 500 ends higher as traders shift from AI to healthcare
item.description: The S&P 500 ended higher on Thursday, springing back from early losses as investors concerned about AI stocks shifted into Eli Lilly, UnitedHealth and other healthcare and consumer stocks.
item.dc:creator: Noel Randewich, Sruthi Shankar
item.content:encoded: The S&P 500 ended higher on Thursday, springing back from early losses as investors concerned about AI stocks shifted into Eli Lilly, UnitedHealth and other healthcare and consumer stocks. Several technology stocks fell, as investors scrutinized AI-related companies whose debt loads leave them vulnerable to rising interest rates. Drugmaker Eli Lilly (LLY.N) gained over 3%, UnitedHealth (UNH.N) added 2.8% and Walmart rose 1.4% after rating upgrades by Deutsche Bank. Those three companies were heavy contributors to the S&P 500's gain for the session. Nvidia (NVDA.O) dipped 1.8% after chip manufacturer TSMC (2330.TW) struck [USN:L1N461004 TEXT:"a cautious note"] on 2027 despite reporting a sixth consecutive record quarterly profit on robust AI-driven demand. Dell Technologies (DELL.N) dropped 6.9% and Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE.N) fell 7.1%, with both server makers adding to sharp losses in the prior session related to worries about AI companies exposed to higher borrowing costs. The yield on 10-year Treasuries retreated but remained near multiyear highs as investors worried about inflation related to high oil prices. "The cost to finance everything, whether it be a new single-family house or a giant data center, is going up, and that has implications for lots of stuff in the stock market," said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management in St. Louis. "The best performing stocks today are the non-cyclical, defensive businesses." The Philadelphia semiconductor index (.SOX) fell 0.9%, down for a seventh straight session. The S&P 500 climbed 0.33% to end the session at 7,744.06 points. The Nasdaq gained 0.08% to 26,713.03 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average rallied 1.08% to 52,177.69 points. Volume on US exchanges was heavy, with 20.7 billion shares traded, compared to an average of 17.6 billion shares over the previous 20 sessions. Eight of the 11 S&P 500 sector indexes rose, led by healthcare (.SPXHC) , up 1.84%, followed by a 1.71% gain in materials (.SPLRCM) . After hitting a record high last week, the S&P 500 remains up about 13% in 2026, with most of that gain fueled by AI-related stocks. The S&P 500 is trading at about 19 times expected earnings, around its lowest level since 2023. The index's relatively low price-to-earnings valuation suggests investors are pricing in an eventual end to the massive earnings growth fueled by AI heavyweights, Ellerbroek said. Data on Thursday showed US producer prices [USN:L1N460127 TEXT:"increased by the most"] in 4-1/2 years in September amid rising goods and services costs, the latest indication of inflation broadening beyond energy products. [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"Hotter-than-expected consumer inflation data"] on Wednesday fueled expectations of further interest-rate hikes by the US Federal Reserve, contributing to a Wall Street selloff. "You've got a little rotation going on in the bigger names, but we've seen this before. It seems this crops up every couple of months and we have the AI concerns," said Joe Saluzzi, co-head of equity trading at Themis Trading in Chatham, New Jersey. Interest rate traders are pricing in a 67% chance the Fed will raise interest rates by its December policy meeting, up from a 62% probability on Wednesday, according to CME's FedWatch tool. Shares of [USN:L4N46023Y TEXT:"Rocket Lab"] (RKLB.O) dropped 6.6% after the space company said the inaugural launch of its new, larger Neutron rocket was delayed until next year. FMC (FMC.N) tumbled over 30% after the agrichemicals company [USN:L4N46114X TEXT:"sharply cut"] its third-quarter outlook. Advancing issues outnumbered falling ones within the S&P 500 (.AD.SPX) by a 3.1-to-1 ratio. The S&P 500 posted 24 new highs and no new lows; the Nasdaq recorded 61 new highs and 393 new lows.

item.title: Ukraine hits Russian refinery as Zelenskiy says 'we're done' with Trump's energy truce
item.description: Ukraine struck a Russian oil refinery on Thursday after President Volodymyr Zelenskiy declared that Kyiv was abandoning a ceasefire covering energy sites announced by US President Donald Trump, and criticised Trump's willingness to strike deals with Moscow.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Flynn, Max Hunder
item.content:encoded: Ukraine struck a Russian oil refinery on Thursday after President Volodymyr Zelenskiy declared that Kyiv was abandoning a ceasefire covering energy sites announced by US President Donald Trump, and criticised Trump's willingness to strike deals with Moscow. By effectively walking away from Trump's demand that Ukraine halt attacks on Russian refineries and openly criticising the US leader, Zelenskiy risks deepening the biggest rift between Kyiv and Washington since Russia's February 2022 invasion of Ukraine. Ukraine's latest target was a refinery in the Ryazan region southeast of Moscow, which is owned by state oil major Rosneft and accounts for nearly 5% of Russia's refinery throughput, helping supply the capital. Regional governor Pavel Malkov said on Telegram that a [USN:S8N44O03I TEXT:"major Ukrainian drone attack"] had caused a fire at the refinery. Russian President Vladimir Putin [USN:L1N4610T1 TEXT:"played down"] the effect of Ukrainian long-range attacks on Russian refineries, saying they had caused "nothing particularly significant." After Trump's surprise announcement on Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to halt attacks on energy sites, Kyiv suspended attacks on Russian refineries, which Trump blames for raising diesel prices on global markets. But in the days that followed, Russia rained down missile and drone strikes, including on energy targets such as power stations, knocking out power to hundreds of thousands of people. Zelenskiy's relations with Trump have been testy, particularly after a February 2025 Oval Office meeting descended into a shouting match. Zelenskiy has since praised Trump and US help for Ukraine, and in recent days said Ukraine fully backed the energy ceasefire despite waves of Russian attacks. PATIENCE RAN OUT In an interview with the Financial Times published on Thursday, Zelenskiy said Ukraine's patience had run out. "The block (on attacking refineries) is out. We're done," he told the newspaper. Zelenskiy also criticised what he saw as Trump's willingness to strike deals with Russia, apparent admiration for Putin and an affinity for those wielding power or considerable wealth. "He (Trump) speaks about it openly and loudly that he loves such people and he respects such people," the FT quoted him as saying. "Because for him people who can be leaders 20 years, 30 years, 40 years, it means they can be very strong." In his comments to the FT, Zelenskiy also said he believed that changes in the capability of the military version of SpaceX's Starlink receptors this week, which curbed Ukraine's ability to pilot its drones, were a policy decision. "It was not a technical problem, it was the will," he told the FT. British Defence Minister Wes Streeting [USN:L1N46110U TEXT:"said on Thursday"] that he and US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth welcomed the restoration of the Starlink service in Ukraine and called for both sides to "move forward in a collective spirit". "We need President Trump engaged on Ukraine. He has been, and the diplomatic track is as important in ending the war as making sure Ukraine has the weapons it needs to see off Russian aggression," he said on Fox News. EU SUMMIT Zelenskiy [USN:L1N46107Z TEXT:"was due to attend"] a European Union summit on Friday and in a series of meetings ahead of the gathering stressed the need to strengthen air defences. In a social media post overnight, SpaceX boss Elon Musk said usage of the military version of Starlink, known as Starshield, was ultimately up to Trump as president of the United States. "Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS," Musk wrote. Although Trump has described the ceasefire as a requirement for both Moscow and Kyiv, his public comments have focused mainly on Ukraine's attacks on Russian refineries, which he said over the weekend had "damn well better stop". Ukrainians worry that the rift could have severe consequences on the battlefield, where the Ukrainian military still depends on technology provided by Washington. Ukrainian officials say that for several days they have not received the usual warnings, which rely on US satellite detectors, from Western allies about incoming Russian missiles,. Trump has denied withholding intelligence. At the same time, military-grade Starlink receptors have stopped working in Ukraine when mounted on fast-moving objects, interfering with the performance of Ukrainian drones that rely on them for onboard guidance systems over Ukrainian territory. A source in Ukraine's defence ministry said on Thursday that the receptors were now working when in motion, but only at speeds of up to 100 miles per hour (160 kph). Ukrainian officials say that is too slow for mid-range attack missions and interceptor drones that defend against Russian drones. Defence experts said, and a Reuters analysis of satellite imagery, meanwhile, [USN:L8N4601YV TEXT:"showed that"] Russia had in just six weeks nearly finished building a major base in southern Russia for launching jet-powered drones. Ukraine has been using its long-range drones to target Russian refineries and logistics in recent months, which it says is its only answer to nearly five years of relentless Russian bombardment. The attacks have caused fuel shortages in Russia. Trump is under pressure to lower fuel prices, with his Republicans facing midterm elections in less than three weeks,. Prices for diesel have reached record highs since he launched a war against Iran in February, though Trump says the Ukrainian attacks are driving up global prices. In the Black Sea, rescuers searched for seven missing sailors after [USN:L8N4610EC TEXT:"drones struck"] two chemical tankers near Romania's Black Sea coast, setting them ablaze in the latest attack on shipping along a vital route used by Ukraine. The Kremlin said on Thursday that Ukraine's targeting of Russian energy infrastructure ran counter to US peace efforts. It said earlier this week that the scope of the energy ceasefire had never been determined and work was ongoing to do so.

item.title: Indonesia's new disaster mitigation chief plans to assess foreign aid to tackle wildfires
item.description: Indonesian authorities said on Thursday they would consider offers of foreign assistance to tackle the country's biggest forest fires in over a decade after President Prabowo Subianto named new disaster management leaders.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Indonesian authorities said on Thursday they would consider offers of foreign assistance to tackle the country's biggest forest fires in over a decade after President Prabowo Subianto named new disaster management leaders. The Southeast Asian nation is facing intense criticism as it struggles to control its most intense wildfires since 2015 after an El Niño-driven drought turned forests and land highly flammable. The fires have been raging for months and hundreds of thousands of people have contracted respiratory illnesses in the worst-hit provinces, while the transboundary haze has also hampered air quality in [USN:L6N4600NO TEXT:"neighbouring countries,"] forcing school closures in Malaysia and East Timor. "The sky yesterday was very yellow ... People's activities are far reduced because of this condition. We hope there will be rain soon that will ease this problem," 46-year-old Adinata, a resident of Palangka Raya city in Central Kalimantan, told Reuters. Dozens of residents in the city, which has been darkened by thick orange smog this week, staged a protest at the governor's office on Thursday, local news reported. Cities in Kalimantan and Sumatra have been choked by haze due to peatland fires, which smoulder slowly beneath the surface and can re-emerge anytime, and also produce thicker smoke. The air pollution index in the regions has far exceeded the "hazardous" level of 300 with the Katingan district of Central Kalimantan registering a reading of nearly 1,600 earlier on Thursday, while the provincial capital Palangka Raya recorded nearly 1,300. PRABOWO ORDERS SHAKEUP Prabowo named army general Kristomei Sianturi as the new head of disaster mitigation agency BNPB, the main body in charge of the firefighting efforts. "I will assess our assets and see what kind of foreign aid we can accelerate," Sianturi said after his inauguration, adding he has been tasked to contain the wildfires "as soon as possible." Malaysia last month had offered three helicopters and an aircraft to help put out the wildfires, but an official earlier this week said Indonesia is [USN:L6N45Z09S TEXT:""still able to handle""] the issue. The president also named forestry ministry official Satyawan Pudyatmoko as chief of a newly formed peatland and mangrove body on Thursday, tasking him with restoring the country's peatland ecosystem and preventing repeated wildfires. "We will restore peatland ecosystems to their former condition," he told reporters. "There are a number of peatland areas that are being prioritised and the president doesn't want any more fires." PEATLAND RESTORATION Peatland protection group Pantau Gambut estimated that out of 24 million hectares of Indonesian peatland, 16 million hectares have been made more fire-prone as a result of ecosystem damage, including extensive deforestation and the depletion of water tables. A 2024 study conducted by Pantau Gambut showed that only 3% of the peatland damaged by fires over the 2015 to 2019 period has been restored into forest, while 54% was converted into monoculture plantations, mainly oil palm. A food estate project in the 1990s was among the causes of peatland degradation, deputy food minister Hanif Faisol Nurofiq said, and the government is aiming to drill wells to rewet peatlands and improve water canal management. Thesa, a 19-year-old university student in Palangka Raya who has been experiencing dizziness due to haze, sought help at a volunteer organization providing oxygen for people exposed to toxic air. "We are being exposed to the smoke everyday... and there is only a fan at my boarding room (to alleviate the smoke)."

item.title: Dollar recedes from 18-month high as bond rally tempers impact of hot inflation data
item.description: The dollar retreated from an 18-month peak on Thursday as investors looked past strong US inflation and spending data to focus on a shakeout in the securities of AI data center firms.
item.dc:creator: Laura Matthews
item.content:encoded: The dollar retreated from an 18-month peak on Thursday as investors looked past strong US inflation and spending data to focus on a shakeout in the securities of AI data center firms. US producer prices rose by the most in 4-1/2 years in September as goods and services costs increased, adding to evidence that inflation pressures are spreading beyond energy. Retail sales [USN:L1N460114 TEXT:"rose more than expected"] last month, lifted by higher gasoline prices, while weekly jobless claims [USN:L1N4600ZS TEXT:"marginally increased"], pointing to resilient consumer demand and a stable labor market. But government bonds rallied and the dollar pulled back, reflecting cautious remarks from Federal Reserve officials that further cooled expectations for an October interest-rate hike. "We have a narrative that is dollar negative based on the idea that inflation at this level and this quick pace is unsustainable," said Juan Perez, director of trading at Monex USA in Washington. "Regardless of no good news on the war front or the equity picture looking pessimistic, the market is anti-USD after a heavy dose of strengthening in the last four weeks. ... The economic stagnation seems to be having more influence in (the) mind of traders." AI COMPANIES' DEBT BURDENS The dollar index , which measures the US currency against a basket of peers, fell 0.45% to 101.99, having hit an 18-month high on Wednesday after US inflation figures came in stronger than expected. That helped the euro bounce 0.56% from an 18-month trough to $1.1218, putting it on track for its biggest daily gain in nearly two months. Sterling strengthened 0.64% to $1.3275 after data showed [USN:L8N4610AT TEXT:"Britain's economy unexpectedly grew"] 0.1% in August. Markets [USN:L6N46100A TEXT:"grew choppy"] after Wednesday's [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"hot US CPI reading"] initially bolstered bets on higher-for-longer Fed rates, while renewed concerns over AI companies' heavy debt burdens fuelled safe-haven flows into Treasuries. "The selloff in chip stocks offers support to bonds, helping keep yields in check despite the inflationary signals," said Uto Shinohara, senior investment strategist at Mesirow Currency Management. Traders now see a 73% chance that the Fed will leave rates unchanged at its October 27-28 meeting, compared with 53% a month ago, CME Group's FedWatch Tool showed. The expected likelihood of a hike [USN:L6N4600VL TEXT:"rose sharply"] after the CPI report, but bets eased after Fed officials including Vice Chair for Supervision [USN:L1N4600EO TEXT:"Michelle Bowman"] and San Francisco Fed President [USN:L6N4601E8 TEXT:"Mary Daly"] said the central bank could wait for more clarity before the meeting. "If yields struggle to extend higher and dollar rallies continue to attract sellers, it will strengthen our conviction that the inflation news is largely absorbed, leaving the balance of risks tilted in favor of risk assets," said Joel Kruger, a market strategist at LMAX Group in London. Investors will also watch remarks from Fed officials including Chair Kevin Warsh at IMF-World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok on Friday for clues on the US central bank's next move. The Australian dollar weakened 0.77% to $0.6919, after [USN:L1N46100L TEXT:"local employment"] unexpectedly slid in September, while the Japanese yen strengthened 0.15% to 158.08 per dollar. "With the Fed entering its blackout period shortly and no tier-one data releases remaining before the meeting, market direction will likely remain driven by geopolitical uncertainty surrounding Russia/Ukraine and Iran, alongside developments in the AI story," said Shinohara.

item.title: Global stocks flat as AI and rate fears hit tech
item.description: An index of global equity markets ended flat on Thursday as concerns about AI spending and higher interest rates fueled further selling in technology and chip stocks.
item.dc:creator: Chibuike Oguh
item.content:encoded: An index of global equity markets ended flat on Thursday as concerns about AI spending and higher interest rates fueled further selling in technology and chip stocks. Investors have been unnerved by valuations of companies in the AI ecosystem as more voices question the sustainability of demand for data centers. On Wall Street, the Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index (.SOX) ended down nearly 1%. The benchmark S&P 500 and the Nasdaq reversed losses in early trade and finished higher, led by healthcare and materials stocks, while the Dow gained 1%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) rose 1.08%, the S&P 500 (.SPX) rose 0.33%, and the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) rose 0.08%. "There's definitely a lot of investor skittishness right now about the path forward for AI," said Amanda Agati, chief investment officer at PNC Financial Services Group. A brutal tech-led selloff had hit stocks overnight in Asia. South Korea's KOSPI index (.KS11) , whose flock of top chipmakers made it one of the main beneficiaries of AI euphoria, plunged almost 8%, while the Nikkei 225 (.N225) fell nearly 5%. "I think the selloff reflects investor caution towards the more vulnerable segment of the AI ecosystem, with tech chiefs advocating a slower pace of frontier model development," said Rong Ren Goh, portfolio manager at Eastspring Investments. "Markets increasingly question the sustainability and trajectory of demand for computing capacity. These concerns are compounded by higher funding costs, which raise the investment hurdle rates of capital-intensive AI infrastructure projects." MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan (.MISX00000PUS) closed 3.12% lower, marking its biggest one-day drop since late July. MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe (.MIWD00000PUS) fell 0.06%. European stocks (.STOXX) erased early-session losses and finished up 0.38%. BOND YIELDS FALL Benchmark 10-year US Treasury yields fell back towards 5% in what was their biggest daily drop in more than a year. US producer prices rose by the most in 4-1/2 years in September as goods and services costs increased, suggesting that inflation pressures are spreading beyond energy. New US [USN:L1N460114 TEXT:"retail sales data"] showed retail sales increased more than expected last month, boosted by higher gasoline prices, but the data also pointed to spending elsewhere remaining moderate. The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes fell 12.58 basis points to 5.064%. DOLLAR DROPS Wednesday's [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"US inflation data"] had once again tweaked expectations for the Fed's rate path, with traders briefly pricing in roughly even odds of a hike this month, before scaling back those bets. Fed funds futures are now pricing an implied 73% probability the US central bank will stay on hold at the end of its next two-day meeting on October 28, little changed from the start of the week, according to the CME Group's FedWatch tool. In the currency markets, the dollar slipped from an 18-month peak. Against the yen it was down 0.21% at 157.98 yen, while the euro was up 0.57% at $1.122 and sterling was 0.63% higher and buying $1.33. In [USN:L1N46101K TEXT:"oil markets"], Brent crude fell 0.13% to settle at $105.92 a barrel as traders weighed up the effects of US sanctions relief on supply against attacks on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Spot gold rose 1.57% to $4,169.48 an ounce.

item.title: US considers removing sanctions on some shadow fleet vessels to cut freight rates, official says
item.description: The Trump administration is considering lifting sanctions on some so-called shadow fleet vessels that have transported oil and petroleum products from countries including Russia, Iran and Venezuela, in an effort to reduce record-high global freight rates, a US official said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Timothy Gardner, Jarrett Renshaw
item.content:encoded: The Trump administration is considering lifting sanctions on some so-called shadow fleet vessels that have transported oil and petroleum products from countries including Russia, Iran and Venezuela, in an effort to reduce record-high global freight rates, a US official said on Wednesday. The discussions come days after President Donald Trump temporarily [USN:S0N43U024 TEXT:"lifted sanctions"] on Russian diesel fuel, a move met with a torrent of criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, [USN:S8N43U03J TEXT:"European"] countries and some of Trump's [USN:L1N45Z0TJ TEXT:"fellow Republicans"] in the US Senate. Both Zelenskiy and the US senators called that move a gift to Russian President Vladimir Putin that would provide Russia with revenue to keep funding its war in Ukraine. The new talks center on the United States potentially allowing "legal oil" to flow on previously sanctioned vessels, the US official said. That means crude or petroleum products not sanctioned by Washington rather than Russian and Iranian oil, which are under punitive measures. The goal is to move more refined products and crude out of the Gulf, the official said. Companies seeking to buy the sanctioned vessels would have to apply to the US Treasury Department for approval of the transactions, the official said. A Treasury Department official told Reuters that the agency undertakes a "thorough review before removing sanctions on any entity." If legitimate buyers want to purchase the vessels and restore them for use by global commercial shipping, Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control "may consider authorizing those transactions and removing sanctions on those vessels on a case-by-case basis," the official said. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said in a video to the World Petroleum Congress in Riyadh this week that the administration was discussing easing sanctions on shadow fleet vessels in an effort to lower record freight rates that have hurt demand for US crude, according to Energy Aspects, a research group. Portions of the remarks were broadcast on social media, but Reuters was not able to obtain the full video or a transcript. The Department of Energy said it was not available. The Department of Energy said any move to relieve sanctions on the shadow fleet would not help Russia move oil or oil products. But Trump's push to move Russian diesel to global markets quickly could put pressure on the departments to allow shipment via the vessels. The White House did not respond immediately to a request for comment. High oil and fuel prices are a risk for Trump in the November 3 midterm elections in which Republicans are hoping to maintain control of both chambers of Congress. He lifted the sanctions on Russian diesel through April 7. RECORD HIGHS Tanker freight rates have [USN:L4N45U0OZ TEXT:"soared to record highs"] as the wars in Iran and Ukraine have stoked inflation and put US crude oil out of reach for Asian refiners, pushing them to seek alternatives from the Middle East and Latin America. Energy Aspects said in a note to clients that easing the sanctions on the shadow fleet would not greatly impact freight rates but could allow more movement of oil in the Middle East. Lifting the sanctions on the tankers, which are mostly old and not well maintained, is "unlikely to add meaningful mainstream fleet capacity overnight, especially as most tankers sanctioned over Russian or Venezuelan links have been actively trading over the past three months," it said in the note. Easing the restrictions "could make a small number of additional tankers available for certain (Strait of) Hormuz shuttle runs," in the waterway between Iran and Oman. Lifting the measures is unlikely to result in a broad easing of freight rates as ship insurers will still be bound by EU and UK regulations, maritime industry sources said.

item.title: Anthropic to add US voting information to Claude before midterms
item.description: Anthropic said on Wednesday it would add official US voting information from nonprofit Democracy Works and election results to its Claude AI chatbot later this month, ahead of the November midterms.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: (This Oct 14 story has been corrected to say that chats about whom or what to vote for accounted for 0.01% of US conversations, not requests for recommendations on how to vote, in paragraph 7.) Anthropic said on Wednesday it would add official US voting information from nonprofit Democracy Works and election results to its Claude AI chatbot later this month, ahead of the [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"November midterms"]. The AI company said its goal was to position Claude as a useful tool for political conversations, while preventing election-related abuse. "Today, conversations that touch broadly on politics, public policy or social issues account for about 5.75% of all conversations in the United States on Claude.ai, our consumer app," the company said in a statement, citing analysis of 250,000 US conversations. The move comes as AI companies increasingly position chatbots as sources of news and information, potentially helping Anthropic draw more users during the election cycle. About 0.51% of Claude conversations are specifically about elections or voting, Anthropic said, adding that it expects political and election-related queries to rise as election day approaches. Later this month, US users seeking voting logistics will receive answers drawn directly from Democracy Works' database of state and local election sources. Anthropic said chats on whom or what to vote for were 0.01% of U.S. conversations.

item.title: Banks, buildings burn as Albania's capital Tirana erupts into student violence
item.description: Tens of thousands of students stormed the streets of Tirana on Wednesday, setting alight a government building and two banks and hurling stones at police during a protest over rising education costs and corruption.
item.dc:creator: Fatos Bytyci
item.content:encoded: Tens of thousands of students stormed the streets of Tirana on Wednesday, setting alight a government building and two banks and hurling stones at police during a protest over rising education costs and corruption. Police responded with water cannons and tear gas to disperse protesters who started a fire at the ministry of education building, overturned garbage cans and smashed the fronts of local businesses, Reuters footage showed. A Raiffeisen Bank branch near the education ministry also caught fire, a Reuters witness said. The protests represent the most violent outburst against Prime Minister Edi Rama, who won a fourth term in office in elections in May last year but has since faced growing discontent at [USN:L6N3ZC0BA TEXT:"perceived graft"] surrounding top officials. Protesters also dismiss opposition figures as unpalatable alternatives. The unrest caps a summer of peaceful protests against Rama, triggered by the proposed development of a [USN:L6N4380FB TEXT:"luxury resort"] along Albania's pristine southern coast backed by US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner which has been [USN:L6N42J18T TEXT:"caught up in legal disputes"]. "This is a revolution. We are tired of peaceful protests. We will not stop until Rama resigns," said Lora, a student who declined to give her last name said as she threw rocks at the police. Others chanted "Resignation" and "Police of crime." WIDER PROTESTS Student organisers said the protest was over conditions at universities, higher education costs, a lack of financial support and employment prospects after graduation. The unrest is part of a broader wave of student activism sweeping Europe over education and living conditions. In France, high school students have staged [USN:L1N45U08J TEXT:"weeks of protests"] and school blockades demanding more teachers and better facilities, arguing that deteriorating school buildings and overcrowded classrooms are undermining education. Albanian media reported that Wednesday's protests spread to universities at Elbasan and Shkodra. The government condemned the violence. "Protesting is a legitimate right, but it cannot be used as an excuse for violence, city destruction or ugly fighting in the middle of the road," Deputy Prime Minister Albana Kociu said on Facebook. "I call on students and every honest citizen who believes in the right to protest: Distance yourself from violence and vandalism!" The police issued a statement calling for calm. "Any person who uses violence, burns or destroys property, or attacks Police officers, bears individual responsibility and will face the law, in accordance with the offences committed," it said.
